title: Option B cannot carry pin map V6 inside its outline: J5 would need 126-144 positions (132 as traced), but the DF40 stops at 120 and no larger 0.35-0.4 mm pair was found.
what: Pin map V6 sends 12 more ASIC lines through J5. If the top chips' SPI latch and clock are tied to the shared ones, it is 8 more, and the ASIC designer's sheet allows that. J5 is already full. Before any added returns it needs 132 positions as traced, or 128 with the shared latch and clock. With enough returns to close LDOB-01, -09 and -24 it needs 144 or 140 (137 or 133 under a looser rule). Hirose makes no DF40 above 120 positions at any height. The largest 0.35-0.4 mm pairs found from five makers have 54-120 positions. The extra contacts therefore need a second connector pair, and that only fits if the head stack grows: about 0.6-2.6 mm longer with two 0.35 mm 100-pin pairs (land pattern not read), 2.2-2.9 mm wider with a DF40 ear, or 4.2 mm longer with a DF40 pair behind J5.
where: Router J5 DF40C-120DS (bottom, 99.783, 120.2) and LDO board J5 DF40C-120DP (top). Router-LDO overlap strip x 85.833-113.733, y 117.634-122.935 (27.9 x 5.3 mm). J5 receptacle body 26.6 mm, land y 118.31-122.09.
evidence: J5_pin_map_V4.csv: 120 = 108 signals + 9 rails + GND 3/65 + AGND 62. known/pinmap_v6_trace.csv, option B: 12 NEW ROUTE lines (J3/J4 pins 2, 4, 6, 8, 24, 58) and 36 renamed lines, each joined to one J5 contact through router_target. V6 as traced = 120 signals + 9 + 3 = 132. Variant: J5.89-92 freed = 128. Both match a review working file (not published) Smallest return sets come from explicit layouts that were checked (rule in scope_checked): 15 returns gives 144 / 140; the looser rule gives 8 returns and 137 / 133. Outline growth figures are in a review working file (not published) A 0.4 mm part with 128-144 positions would be 28.2-31.4 mm long (A = 0.2n + 2.6) against the 27.9 mm strip. Moving every regulator onto the router saves only 6-8 positions.
source: Hirose DF40 Series catalogue, contents as of 2/2024: p.4 stacking-height table, p.6 position list, p.8 receptacle dimensions. Distributor copy https://doc.7-el.ru/d/df40.pdf, identical to a review working file (not published); product page https://www.hirose.com/en/product/series/DF40. Panasonic AXE800124A https://industry.panasonic.com/global/en/products/control/connector/base-fpc/number/axe800124a and AXE700127 https://industry.panasonic.com/global/en/products/control/connector/base-fpc/number/axe700127. Kyocera AVX 5861 https://www.kyocera-avx.com/product/5861-series/. Molex https://www.molex.com/en-us/products/series-chart/51338, JAE https://www.mouser.com/datasheet/3/356/1/MB_0356E_WP26DK.pdf and Hirose BM23FR https://www.hirose.com/en/product/series/BM23FR: these three are from search summaries only. Project files: known/pinmap_v6_trace.csv, inputs/ldo_b/V2_record/J5_pin_map_V4.csv, inputs/ldo_b/V2_fit/fit_b_v2.json, exports/ldo_b_router/board.json, exports/ldo_b_ldo/board.json.
consequence: Option B as drawn cannot connect 12 of the V6 lines (8 in the variant). Keeping it means a new router-LDO joint with two mated pairs, a larger head stack and new layouts of both boards. Option A needs no connector change for V6: the new lines use 12 of its 15 spare J1/J2 contacts. Its re-routing is a separate open item.
suggested_action: Make the keep-or-drop decision on these numbers. If Option B is kept, choose one two-pair layout (DF40 ear east of the lower ASIC board, or two A35S pairs once Panasonic's land drawing is read). Then re-pin J5 with the return rule and redo both layouts.

title: The LT3582's VIN pin lacks the local capacitor its data sheet requires, so LDOB-18 should be major, as LDOA-06 is.
what: LDOB-18 was rated minor because the LT3582 data sheet had not been read. The data sheet makes VIN pin 5 both the chip supply and the source of the inverting converter's power switch, requires a local ceramic bypass capacitor on it, and its suggested layout puts the input capacitor right at pin 5. On the B LDO board pin 5 sits alone on a small L6 copper island, fed only through one microvia, 8.6 mm of 0.3 mm L5 trace and a second microvia in C1's pad. This misses a datasheet requirement exactly like LDOA-06 (major) on Option A; the B block is the A layout moved 5.81 mm in y.
where: LDO board V2 (ldo_b_ldo), bottom: U1 LT3582EUD-12 pin 5 /VIN_3V3 at (100.75, 149.85) on a 2.36 mm2 L6 island (bbox 100.53-101.68 x 149.34-151.59); 0.2 mm L6 stub to microvia (100.75, 150.66) L5-L6; 0.3 mm L5 trace to microvia (108.95, 151.66) in the C1.1 pad. C1, C2 (100 nF, 110.4, 150.93) and C11 (4.7 uF, 103.125, 146.11) sit on the main L6 VIN pour.
evidence: exports/ldo_b_ldo/zones.csv: L6_PWR_VIN_3V3 has two separate fills, 113.61 mm2 and 2.36 mm2; a pcbnew zone query (a review working file (not published)) shows the 2.363 mm2 piece holds only U1.5 and the 113.614 mm2 piece holds C1.1, C2.1, C11.1 and L11.1. exports/ldo_b_ldo/board.json: L6 (100.75,149.85)-(100.75,150.66) w 0.2; L5 (100.75,150.66)-(101.75,151.66)-(108.95,151.66) w 0.3, 1.414 + 7.2 = 8.61 mm; both vias 0.10 mm drill, 0.26 mm pad. Copper path to C1 is about 0.8 + 1.4 + 7.2 = 9.4 mm; C11 is reached only through C1 and the pour. Option A V12 has U1.5 at (100.75, 144.04): the same block, offset 5.81 mm. Data sheet: p.8, pin 5 is the source of the PMOS power switch and needs a local ceramic bypass; p.19, a 4.7 uF input capacitor is sufficient; p.21 Figure 12 (rendered to a review working file (not published)) shows CIN between VIN pin 5 and GND at the package; p.3, the 490-720 mA inverting switch current limit flows through this feed. Merge re-check (12 Nov): the same tracks and vias in board.json, and the p.8 requirement in the saved text copy.
source: ADI LT3582/LT3582-5/LT3582-12 data sheet 3582512fb Rev B: p.3 (inverting switch current limit), p.8 Pin Functions (VIN pin 5), p.19 (Capacitor Selection), p.21 (Board Layout Considerations, Figure 12), https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/3582512fb.pdf. analog.com was unreachable on 12 Nov 2026 (timed out after 60 s), so it was read from the saved copies a review working file (not published) (SHA-256 af3660d7..., the same file LDOA-07 cites) and 3582512fb.txt in the same folder. Project records: known/ldo_b.json LDOB-18; known/ldo_a.json LDOA-06; known/fix_plans_11nov_evening_on_V3.json (LDOB-18 and LDOA-06 plans and the critic's conflict note).
consequence: The inverting channel's pulsed switch current (up to the 490-720 mA limit at start-up) flows through a few nH of feed, giving spikes of a few tenths of a volt at VIN at each switch edge (LDOA-06 estimate). That can disturb the converter's switch-current sensing or make it switch erratically, and it adds noise and ripple to VIN_3V3, which feeds every ASIC LDO and the Frontend joint.
suggested_action: Treat LDOB-18 as major and apply the LDOA-06 fix on the B LDO board before any B order: place a 1-4.7 uF X5R ceramic (optionally with 100 nF) on the pin-5 island with its ground via beside U1's EP vias, or merge the island into the main L6 VIN pour next to C11, then re-run DRC. The fix plans disagree on the part (LDOB-18 plan: 0402 C12; LDOA-06 plan: 0201 C18, because an 0402 does not fit the matching strip on A), so settle one part and placement for both options.

title: The Option B LDO board repeats U8, U9 and U10 with no clamp, bleeder or REF_VCM load, so LDOA-08, LDOA-09 and LDOA-14 apply to B; any power-down with no or light ASIC load, on or off the head, takes U10's OUT more than 0.3 V below IN.
what: The B LDO board has the same U9/U10 cells, capacitors and RC enable as Option A, with no clamp or bleeder, so LDOA-08 and LDOA-09 apply unchanged. The Option A review listed this for B as not checked. On B the LDO board and Frontend come off the head as one module. Whenever that module is powered off the head (bench work, firmware loading, or the cable pulled after unplugging), VSS10 has no load at all. After power loss, U10's own ground current then pulls its input above its output while the RC keeps it enabled; LDOA-09's model shows this exceeds the LT3094's 0.3 V OUT-to-IN limit in every no-load case. The same unplugged module also runs U8 (REF_VCM, 0.75 V) below its 10 uA minimum load (LDOA-14).
where: LDO board V2. U10 LT3094 (107.55, 132.15): IN pins 1/2/13 and PGFB on /STIM_PRE_NEG (C1001 10 uF, plus C21 22 uF through JP2); OUT 11/12 and OUTS 10 on /ASIC_VSS10 (C1002 22 uF, C1004 10 uF, J5.73 only); EN on /EN_ASIC_RAILS (R1 10k, C3 4.7 uF). Also U9 on /ASIC_VDD10 (C902, J5.55) and U8 on /ASIC_REF_VCM (C802, J5.60).
evidence: exports/ldo_b_ldo/netlist.xml: /ASIC_VSS10 = C1002.1, C1004.1, J5.73, U10.10/11/12; /STIM_PRE_NEG = C1001.1, JP2.2, TP9.1, U10.1/2/5/13; no diode, resistor or load on VSS10, VDD10 or REF_VCM except J5 (84/84 parts equal Option A per known/ldo_b.json). With the module off the head J5.73 is open, so the only VSS10 load is U10. The LT3094 GND current (2.35 mA typical) flows into the input node. With about 10-13 uF effective input capacitance (32 uF nominal 25 V 0805 at 12 V; derating assumed, not from a vendor curve), IN rises about 0.2 V/ms. It passes OUT + 0.3 V about 10-13 ms after power loss, while R1/C3 hold EN for about 49 ms (LDOA-09). LDOA-09's model gives OUT more than 0.5 V below IN in every case at 0-0.5 mA load, for 15-40 ms, with 0.5-2.6 mA in the substrate diode. known/ldo_a.json not_checked: 'whether Option B shares the power-down polarity issue: not reviewed'. The B record has no 'cable last on, first off' rule; the fix plans only propose one under LDOB-04. Merge re-check: the nets above, and C1001 10 uF / C21 22 uF (both 25 V X5R 0805), as stated in netlist.xml and parts.csv.
source: ADI LT3094 data sheet Rev 0: p.3 Absolute Maximum Ratings (OUT, OUTS and SET with respect to IN, -0.3 V); p.4 GND pin current (2.35 mA typical); p.15 Pin Functions (OUTS-to-IN substrate diode). https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/lt3094.pdf. ADI LT3042 Rev A (3042fa), Electrical Characteristics, Minimum Load Required (10 uA below 1 V, Note 13). https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/lt3042.pdf. Both read from saved copies in a review working file (not published) because analog.com timed out. Project records LDOA-08, LDOA-09, LDOA-14 (known/ldo_a.json).
consequence: U10's substrate diode conducts outside ADI's absolute maximum at every power-down of a module off the head, with unknown long-term effect. The REF_VCM regulator may be unstable whenever the module runs off the head.
suggested_action: Add LDOA-08, LDOA-09 and LDOA-14 to the B list and apply whatever fix is chosen for Option A to the B LDO board, since the parts are the same. Until then, add 'never power the module off the head; cable last on, first off' to the B handling rules.

title: J5 has only 2 GND and 1 AGND contacts for 108 single-ended ASIC lines, so return paths are long and shared.
what: Every signal needs a return current path back to its source, normally through a nearby ground pin where it crosses a connector. On Option B the 108 single-ended 1.5 V lines through J5 (88 ASIC outputs, 20 FPGA outputs) share 2 GND contacts and 1 AGND contact: 54 signals per GND contact, or 36 per return contact if AGND is counted, and many signals sit far from any of them. A long, shared return adds inductance, so when many lines switch together the local ground jumps (ground bounce) and lines couple to each other; the most likely failure is a false edge on one of the eight CLK32MHz_Out capture clocks, which switch at the same moment as their data. The same lines already cross the ASIC board's DF40-80 connectors in both options at about 15 signals per return contact, so J5 is roughly 2 to 2.5 times worse than a crossing they already make, and the size of the effect is unknown because the ASIC drive strength and edge rate are not specified.
where: Option B router (J5 DF40C-120DS, bottom) and LDO board (J5 DF40C-120DP, top): GND pins 3 and 65, AGND pin 62; worst signal J5.120 (ASIC5_DATA1). Router: J5.65 reaches the L3 GND plane only through a 3.60 mm x 0.20 mm L6 (B.Cu) track to a via in the J4.46 pad at (100.783, 115.10); J5.3 through a 1.91 mm x 0.15 mm L6 track to a via at (87.383, 117.75).
evidence: J5_pin_map_V4.csv and exports/ldo_b_router, exports/ldo_b_ldo pads.csv: 120 pins = 108 signals + 9 rails + 2 GND (3, 65) + 1 AGND (62), 0.4 mm pitch. Pad-centre distance from each signal to the nearest J5 GND pad: LDO board median 4.65 mm, max 11.13 mm (J5.120), 48 signals over 5 mm, 16 over 8 mm; router median 4.77 mm, max 11.23 mm, 51 over 5 mm, 16 over 8 mm; counting AGND the median is 4.40 mm. Comparisons: LDO board J1/J2 carry the same 108 signals on 14 GND (7.7 per contact); router J3/J4 and Option A J3/J4 each carry 58 signals on 2 GND + 2 AGND (29 per GND contact); the ASIC board's DF40C-80 has 61 signal or pass-through pins on 2 DGND + 2 AGND, worst signal about 9 mm from a DGND pin (inputs/asic/J3_pinout__J3_Pinout.csv, J3_pinout__Summary.csv). exports/ldo_b_router/board.json: the two GND tracks above, 3 GND vias, GND pour only on L3 (269.3 mm2). LDO board: a GND via within 0.15 mm of each J5 GND pad, GND planes on L3/L4. Frontend_V46_pins_V2.xdc sets these lines to LVCMOS15. Estimate, not derived from any file: 40 of 88 ASIC outputs switching together at about 5 mA with 2 ns edges (0.1 A/ns) through an assumed 1-2 nH shared return gives at most 0.1-0.2 V; 1-2 nH is a high-end guess for three contacts in parallel plus vias.
source: Engineering judgement (signal-to-return ratio and loop inductance across a board-to-board connector). AMD DS181 Artix-7 data sheet, LVCMOS15 input thresholds: not checked against the datasheet (docs.amd.com returned 404). DF40 contact inductance: not given in the Hirose catalogue data read.
consequence: Possible capture errors or crosstalk on the 32 MHz data and clock lines, mainly false edges on the CLK32MHz_Out capture clocks. Option B adds this crossing on top of the ASIC-board crossing both options already make; the size of the risk is unknown until the ASIC driver is characterised.
suggested_action: Decide before ordering: add return contacts on J5 (more GND/AGND pins or a small second connector) so no signal is far from a return, or simulate or bench-test the J5 crossing with the ASIC driver and accept it in writing. On the router, add GND vias to L3 at the J5.65 and J5.3 pads.
v2note: Under pin map V6, which the ASIC boards V4 require, Option B must carry 120 single-ended lines across J5 instead of 108: 88 ASIC outputs and 32 FPGA outputs, including 12 new lines from router J3/J4 pins 2/4/6/8/24/58. Today's J5 already uses all 120 of its contacts (blocker A-P), so keeping it and accepting it after a bench test is no longer possible, and the return count must be set when J5 is replaced (2 x DF40C-80 would leave 31 returns, not 43, and the LDO-board J1/J2 and router J3/J4 pin maps change). The other crossings also get worse: the router J3/J4 carry 64 signals (not 58) and each ASIC V4 DF40C-80 carries 67 signal pins (not 61), each on 2 DGND + 2 AGND. The far-chip CLK32 move onto today's ASIC3/4/7/8_DATA8 lanes (J5.81/7/82/34), so the J5 return fixes of LDOB-02/09/24 and the far-clock parts of LDOB-09/23/25/32 must be redone on the re-laid boards. See LDOB-55.

title: 89 of 108 Option B lanes run over AGND on one board and GND on the other, pushing digital return into AGND.
what: A fast signal's return current flows in the plane right next to its track. On the router, lanes on L5 and L6 lie over the L4 AGND plane and lanes on L1 and L2 over the L3 GND plane; on the LDO board, L1 lanes lie over the L2 AGND plane and L2/L5 lanes over GND, so 89 of the 108 lanes through J5 spend part of their length over AGND and part over GND. Their return current must change ground net at layer-change vias inside each board and at the far ends: at J1/J2, where the Frontend side is GND only, and at router J3/J4, where AGND meets the ASIC board's AGND pins instead of its digital ground (DGND). The slow part of that current can cross only through NT1, a net tie (a deliberate small copper bridge between two nets) on the LDO board, and the fast edge part crosses through the capacitance between the adjacent GND and AGND planes, which is not a low-impedance path; either way digital switching current lands on AGND, the recording reference.
where: Router: L5 (In4.Cu, 25 signal nets) and L6 (B.Cu, 32 signal nets) over L4 AGND; L1/L2 over L3 GND. LDO board: L1 over L2 AGND; L2/L5 over L3/L4 GND. NT1 (NetTie-2_SMD_Pad0.5mm, 0.5 x 1.0 mm bridge) on the LDO board underside at (100.58, 126.81). J5 GND pins 3 and 65, AGND pin 62. ASIC board J3/J4: AGND pins 42/44, DGND pins 46/48.
evidence: board.json lane copper: router L1 300, L2 255, L5 231, L6 278 mm, so 509 mm references AGND and 555 mm GND; LDO board L1 382 mm (357 mm over filled L2 AGND), L2 338 mm, L5 989 mm. Per-lane majority reference: 57 lanes over AGND on one board and GND on the other, 32 the reverse, 19 over GND on both (both re-checks agree on these counts). One re-check traced the 57 as the 44 ASIC1-4 lanes (router J4) plus 13 shared lanes, over AGND on the LDO board's L1 and GND on the router, and the 32 as 31 ASIC5-8 lanes plus STIM_CHB, the reverse; the original finding had these directions swapped. The 19 GND-only lanes include 10 of the 11 ASIC6 lanes. NT1 is the only GND-AGND joint on either board; its AGND side reaches the L2 plane through 17.22 mm of L6/L5 track and a microvia plus buried-via chain. Neither B board file has a stack-up block; with Option A's JLC stack (JLCH061611Y1-1078) the router L3-L4 plane pair would be about 13 pF (about 380 Ohm at 32 MHz) and the LDO board L2-L3 pair about 120 pF. exports/asic netlist: /AGND and /DGND are separate nets.
source: Engineering judgement (return current follows the adjacent reference plane; a change of reference net needs a nearby low-impedance path between the nets). inputs/asic/ASIC_Reference/ASIC_REFERENCE.md: the historical FPC carried the 23 signals with 27 DGND conductors and no AGND.
consequence: Digital switching current from up to 89 lanes, 32 MHz clocks among them, is injected into AGND and into the ASIC boards' AGND pins, raising noise on the recording ground and crosstalk between lanes; nothing is measured, so the size is unknown. Changing the plane assignment after fabrication costs a spin of both boards.
suggested_action: Before ordering, choose one ground strategy for the lane field, for example swap the router's L3/L4 nets so L5/L6 lanes reference GND and re-reference the LDO board's L1 lanes to GND; then recheck against the J5 return-pin count.
v2note: LDOB-03 is broader than stated and stays major. The ASIC boards V4 themselves run the chip output lanes over AGND and analogue rail planes: on the far board, 65 % of the 168 mm is on In4 between REF_VDD and VDD_DRIVER/VDD10 (about 60 % with both plane fills present) and 25 % is on F.Cu over In1 AGND (about 20 % over fill); on the near board, 32 % of the 135 mm is on F.Cu over AGND (about 27 % over fill). Each port has only AGND 42/44 and DGND 46/48, and no part joins AGND to DGND on either ASIC board, so the fix plan's re-plan of the B boards alone cannot keep lane returns on GND/DGND from end to end. The lane reference and the return contacts must be chosen for the Option B boards and the ASIC boards together (R2S-05, A-6, ASIC reference U04). That decision belongs in the Option B re-layout that pin map V6 already forces.

title: On the B LDO board the 14 Frontend GND contacts reach the GND planes through only three 0.10 mm laser vias.
what: J1 and J2 carry the return current of all 108 ASIC lanes, plus the 3.3 V supply return, back to the Frontend on 14 GND contacts. On the B LDO board those contacts are joined by thin top-layer traces about 10 mm long. They drop to the L3/L4 GND planes through only three small laser vias: one serves all seven J2 grounds and two serve J1. This is the same copper that Option A's review rated major (LDOA-05), but it is not on the B list, and on B it sits in series with J5's two GND contacts. LDOB-01's comparison (J1/J2 at 7.7 signals per return contact) is therefore optimistic.
where: LDO board V2, L1. J2 GND pins 14/15/27/34/41/50/66 (x 107.4/110.11, y 128.41-138.81) use 0.15 mm stubs to a 0.2 mm spine at x 108.75, then laser via (108.75, 138.81) L1-L2, 0.6 mm of L2, and buried via (108.75, 139.41). J1's same pins use the spine at x 91.25, laser via (91.25, 138.81) and buried via (91.25, 139.41). J1.50 also has laser via (89.9, 135.61), 4.1 mm of 0.15 mm L2 track and buried via (94.0, 135.61).
evidence: exports/ldo_b_ldo/board.json: 27 GND vias (19 through, 4 buried L2-L5, 3 laser L1-L2, 1 laser L5-L6); only the three L1-L2 laser vias touch the J1/J2 GND copper on L1 (the through vias sit at J5.3, J5.65, TP5 and the converter). GND copper on L1 is two 10.40 mm x 0.2 mm spines plus 1.35 mm stubs; zones.csv has GND only on L3/L4. A pcbnew read-only connectivity check (a review working file (not published)) with via (108.75, 138.81) removed leaves J2.14 reaching only 7 of the 44 GND pads (the seven J2 grounds); the merge repeated it on a hash-identical copy of the board (a review working file (not published)): 44 of 44 with the via, 7 of 44 without. A microstrip estimate gives about 0.16-0.45 nH/mm for the spine, so about 2-5 nH shared by seven pins; LDOA-05 gives 2.5-7.7 nH for the identical Option A geometry, which is 5.81 mm north. The B return chain is ASIC DGND, router J3/J4.46/48, router L3, router J5.3/65 stubs (LDOB-01a), LDO J5 vias, LDO L3/L4, these three vias, then J1/J2.
source: Engineering judgement (return-path continuity at board-to-board connectors). Project records: known/ldo_a.json LDOA-05 (same geometry on Option A V12, major); known/ldo_b.json LDOB-01 evidence (J1/J2 counted as 14 return contacts). Files: exports/ldo_b_ldo/board.json, zones.csv, boards/ldo_b_ldo/FPGA_LDO_B_LDO_Layout_V2.kicad_pcb.
consequence: Switching return current from the lanes shares 2-5 nH of ground path at the Frontend joint. That adds ground bounce and crosstalk at the FPGA inputs on top of the J5 bottleneck (LDOB-01/09). One defective laser via disconnects all seven J2 grounds from the LDO board's planes.
suggested_action: Apply LDOA-05's fix to the B LDO board as well: put a via (laser plus buried, or a through via) in or beside each J1/J2 GND pad down to L3/L4, then re-run DRC.

title: Neither Option B board file names a JLC stack-up, so the 0.10 mm laser vias are not tied to a valid template.
what: A stack-up is the list of copper and insulating layers, with thicknesses, that the factory builds. Both Option B board files carry only KiCad's generic 1.6 mm thickness and no stack-up block, while Option A V12 names JLC template JLCH061611Y1-1078; the B boards were built from Option A V11, before that template was added. JLC's laser microvias (0.10 mm holes) need the outer prepreg (the insulating bonding layer under the outer copper) to be no thicker than the hole, and some of JLC's own general-use templates break that rule, so a template must be named before ordering. The router's via set (laser L1-L2 and L5-L6, through vias, no buried vias) is a standard JLC structure, and the through vias in the DF40 pads rely on epoxy fill and capping, which JLC lists as the default for six-layer boards but which should still be written in the order note, as Option A did.
where: boards/ldo_b_router/FPGA_LDO_B_Router_Layout_V2.kicad_pcb and boards/ldo_b_ldo/FPGA_LDO_B_LDO_Layout_V2.kicad_pcb (thickness 1.6, no stack-up block). Through vias in DF40 pads: router J3 22, J4 22, J5 60 (104); LDO board J5 64.
evidence: grep '(stackup': router 0, LDO board 0, Option A V12 1; exports/ldo_b_*/stackup.txt empty; Option A 1.584 mm with 0.071 mm 1078 prepreg (inputs/ldo_a/V12_checks/JLC_stackup_JLCH061611Y1-1078.json, which rejects 2116 templates at 0.112 mm). exports/*/vias.csv: router 21 laser L1-L2 and 42 laser L5-L6 (0.10/0.26 mm), 86 through (0.15/0.35 mm), no buried; LDO board 101 laser L1-L2, 26 laser L5-L6, 67 buried L2-L5 (0.20/0.40 mm), 107 through; no stacked vias. JLC template list (6 layers, 1.6 mm, HDI): 369 templates; 30 match the router's via set, including general-use JLCH061611N1-1078A (1.56 mm, 0.071 mm outer prepreg); general-use JLCH061611N1-2116B (0.112 mm outer prepreg) breaks the depth rule; JLCH061611Y1-1078 matches the LDO board. In-pad via copper to the next pad: 0.125 mm on 0.20 mm pads, 0.110 mm on 0.23 mm pads. Smallest laser-via copper to board edge: LDO board 0.415 mm, router 1.455 mm (JLC minimum 0.35 mm). A JLC news page gives 0.2-0.5 mm for the in-pad fill, against 0.15-0.55 mm on the capabilities page. Fit effect of 1.56-1.57 mm against the assumed 1.6 mm is 0.03-0.04 mm; the +/-10 % thickness tolerance applies to any template.
source: JLCPCB HDI PCB capabilities FAQ (blind via 0.075-0.15 mm, dielectric 0.05-0.127 mm, blind via depth to diameter 1:1 or less; through-via fill not stated), https://jlcpcb.com/help/article/hdi-pcb-capabilities-faq ; JLCPCB HDI fabrication page (with or without buried vias), https://jlcpcb.com/pcb-fabrication/hdi-pcb ; JLCPCB PCB capabilities, Via-in-Pad Process (epoxy filled and capped is the default for 6+ layers, 0.15-0.55 mm vias), https://jlcpcb.com/capabilities/pcb-capabilities ; JLC stack-up template list from jlcpcb.com.
consequence: An order that picks a wrong general-use template, such as a 2116 stack, would break JLC's laser-via depth rule and be refused or re-engineered. Leaving the via fill out of the order note leaves the J5 solder joints dependent on JLC's default.
suggested_action: Name a JLC template in each B board file and its order note (JLCH061611Y1-1078 for the LDO board, a 1078-prepreg template such as JLCH061611N1-1078A for the router) and request filled, capped via-in-pad in the order note, as Option A V12 did.
verification: Upheld after a third independent check

title: Five router rail pours run under 18 other-net J5 contacts, inside the strip Hirose reserves for each net.
what: Each contact of the DF40C-120DS socket lies along the board surface inward of its solder pad, only 0 to 0.13 mm above the board. Hirose's drawing marks the strip from the pad's inner end to 0.75 mm from the connector centre line as an area where only copper of that contact's own circuit may be placed. On the router's bottom layer, five rail pours reach 0.245 mm into this strip under 18 contacts of other nets, with only solder mask between pour and contact. KiCad DRC does not flag it because the footprint has no keep-out.
where: Router (ldo_b_router) J5 DF40C-120DS on B.Cu (L6), centre (99.783, 120.2). ASIC_VDD_CGEN pour under J5.4 (BOARD3_CLK), J5.6; ASIC_DVDD under J5.49, 51, 55 (VDD10), 57 (VDD_DRIVER); ASIC_REF_VCM under J5.56, 58, 62 (AGND), 64; ASIC_REF_VDD under J5.68, 70 (VDD_FE), 74, 76; ASIC_VDD_ADC under J5.71, 73 (VSS10), 77, 79.
evidence: boards/ldo_b_router/FPGA_LDO_B_Router_Layout_V2.kicad_pcb, checked with pcbnew scripts (a review working file (not published)): pads 0.2 x 0.7 mm at |dy| 1.54 mm, inner end at 1.19 mm. Band per pad = pad column, |dy| 0.75-1.19 mm, 0.088 mm2. Saved B.Cu fills of another net overlap the band at exactly 18 pads, 0.045-0.048 mm2 each, reaching |dy| 0.75-0.995 mm (zone clearance 0.2 mm stops the fill 0.195 mm short of the pad). No other-net tracks or vias in any band. pad_to_mask_clearance 0; no rule areas; .kicad_dru has only via rules.
source: Hirose DF40C-120DS-0.4V(51) drawing EDC-317850-51-00 rev 0, sheet 1/2: recommended pattern (3.78 / 2.38 / 1.5 MAX), note 2, section A-A (contact standoff 0.05 +0.08/-0.05 mm); https://www.hirose.com/en/product/p/CL0684-4108-1-51 (drawing_2d). DF40 catalogue p.8 note 3 (insulation area).
consequence: A mask defect or wear under a contact shorts a rail to a neighbouring contact, for example VSS10 under J5.73 or VDD10 (about 9 V) under J5.55, or a rail onto ASIC data and clock lines, which can damage all eight ASICs on the shared rails. The added capacitance is negligible (about 0.05 pF per contact).
suggested_action: Add a B.Cu keep-out strip from |dy| 0.75 to 1.19 mm on each side of the J5 centre line (or an equivalent .kicad_dru rule) so the five pours stay out of other-net contact columns, then refill and re-run DRC.

title: Router J4 and Option A J4 run other-net tracks under the DF40C-80DS contacts, inside Hirose's own-net strip.
what: The 80-pin DF40 socket drawing has the same strip inward of each pad (0.75 to 1.19 mm from the connector centre line) where only copper of that contact's own circuit may be placed. On the router and on Option A, 0.1 mm bottom-layer tracks fanning in between the J4 pad rows lie in this strip under contacts of rails, grounds and signals, with only solder mask between track and contact. DRC does not catch it because the footprint has no rule area. Router J5, Frontend J1/J2 and ASIC board J3 are clean.
where: J4 DF40C-80DS-0.4V(51), B.Cu, centre (99.783, 113.518), on both boards. Router (ldo_b_router): ASIC1_READ at dy +0.86 (x 98.98-107.78) under J4.36-J4.80 even (ASIC_VDD10, VDD_DRIVER, REF_VCM, AGND, GND, VDD_FE, REF_VDD, ASIC_VSS10, VDD_ADC, NC, ASIC3 signals); STIM_CLK_SHARED at dy -0.74 (x 102.58-109.38) under J4.55-J4.79 odd; STIM_START_SHARED at dy -0.94 (x 102.98-109.58) under J4.57-J4.79 odd. Option A (ldo_a): the same three tracks at dy +0.842, -0.758, -0.958, plus ASIC2_DATA1 at dy -0.958 (x 89.11-98.38) under J4.1-J4.31 odd.
evidence: boards/ldo_b_router/FPGA_LDO_B_Router_Layout_V2.kicad_pcb and boards/ldo_a/FPGA_LDO_A_Layout_V12.kicad_pcb via pcbnew and board.json (a review working file (not published)): other-net track copper in the band under 36 of 80 router J4 contacts and 52 of 80 Option A J4 contacts. STIM_CLK_SHARED copper edge is at |dy| 0.79 mm, only 0.04 mm into the band (0.058 mm on Option A); the other tracks are well inside. Pour edges also enter the band: ASIC_VDD_CGEN at router NC pads 3 and 5, ASIC_DVDD at Option A pads 30 and 32. Mask margin 0, no mask graphics in the footprint. Router J5, Frontend J1/J2 (70DS) and ASIC board J3 (80DS): 0.
source: Hirose DF40C-*DS-0.4V(51) drawing EDC3-311352-00, sheet 1/2, recommended pattern (3.78 / 2.38 / 1.5 MAX) and note 2; DF40 catalogue (Aug 2022), p.4, 1.5 mm receptacle recommended PCB layout, note 3; https://www.hirose.com/en/product/series/DF40
consequence: A mask breach under one contact puts ASIC_VDD10, ASIC_VSS10 (about 9 V) or another rail onto ASIC1_READ or the shared STIM lines, which go straight to FPGA and ASIC pins. Both boards miss the vendor's land-pattern rule.
suggested_action: Under J4, move ASIC1_READ, STIM_START_SHARED, STIM_CLK_SHARED (and ASIC2_DATA1 on Option A) so the track copper edge stays inside |dy| 0.75 mm (centreline at or below 0.70 mm for 0.1 mm track) or onto an inner layer, then re-run DRC; Option A's order files would need regenerating.

title: Option B's plug-in module is held to the head only by the J5 DF40 pair, which is rated for 30 mating cycles.
what: Neither Option B board has any drilled hole, so there is no screw, standoff or clip. The only mechanical link between the removable module (the LDO board with the Frontend, the HDMI plug and the cable load) and the part that stays on the head (the router with four ASIC boards) is the J5 DF40C-120 pair, while Hirose asks for another form of board support and rates the DF40 for 30 mating cycles. Per the project record the LDO board and Frontend come off together, so a routine removal uses one cycle on J5 only; the worn half is the router's DF40C-120DS socket, which stays on the head with the ASIC boards, and removal once per session would use the rating in about a month. The missing holes are not specific to Option B: Option A, the Frontend and the ASIC board have none either, so retention is a decision for the whole head stack.
where: Router J5 DF40C-120DS (bottom, 99.783, 120.2), J3 DF40C-80DP, J4 DF40C-80DS; LDO board J5 DF40C-120DP (top), J1/J2 DF40C-70DP mated to Frontend J1/J2 DF40C-70DS. Router outline 27.9 x 12.62 mm, LDO board 27.9 x 35.30 mm; the ASIC boards reach about 10.3 mm past the router's north edge.
evidence: exports/ldo_b_router/pads.csv (299 pads) and exports/ldo_b_ldo/pads.csv (538 pads): all drill 0; board_stats.txt: Through hole 0 and NPTH 0 on both; parts.csv (11 and 75 parts): no mounting-hole footprint; Edge.Cuts has no inner cut-out. Other boards: Option A 593 pads, none drilled; Frontend drilled pads only the 4 Micro-HDMI J3 shell slots; ASIC board 1 drilled pad (J1). Hirose DF40 catalogue: durability 30 mating cycles, 90 mOhm max afterwards (product specifications item 7); provide another form of support (operating precautions item 6, confirmed by one re-check, not extractable by the other); headers of 60 positions or more lack the concave detail that adds mating strength (note 2 of the header table). Records: inputs/notes/fpga-ldo-v14.md says the router stays on, the LDO + Frontend module is removable and needs retention; the V2 record's open list has no retention item.
source: Hirose DF40 series catalogue, product specifications item 7 (Durability) and operating precautions item 6, read from the DigiKey-hosted copy https://mm.digikey.com/Volume0/opasdata/d220001/medias/docus/7138/26_PdfFile_126404.pdf (hirose.com returned 403; edition label and page numbers not confirmed); https://www.hirose.com/en/product/pr/df40/
consequence: Shock, cable pull or handling torque on the module goes straight into 0.4 mm-pitch solder joints and J5 contacts, and frequent removal wears out the router socket attached to the ASIC boards on the head. How fast depends on the removal rate, which is not recorded.
suggested_action: Before the B order, decide how often the module will be removed and what holds it to the head (holes and standoffs, a housing clamp or adhesive), and add holes or keep-outs if needed; if removal will exceed about 30 cycles, choose a higher-cycle connector for J5.

title: Two mated DF40 pairs join the Frontend and the FPGA-LDO board, and under pin map V6 Option B's J5, unplugged at every module removal, would need a second pair too, which Hirose advises against.
what: Hirose's DF40 drawing asks designers not to use more than one mated connector pair between two stacked (sandwiched) boards, because misalignment between the pairs can break connectors during or after mating. The Frontend mates to the FPGA-LDO board through two 70-pin pairs, J1 and J2, in Option A and on the Option B LDO board; J5 alone joins the Option B LDO board and router, which meets the advice. No board in the stack has a mounting hole, so only the contacts take misalignment and handling loads. The project's parts review V21 already notes this caution.
where: Frontend J1/J2 (DF40C-70DS) mating with FPGA-LDO Option A J1/J2 and Option B LDO board J1/J2 (DF40C-70DP).
evidence: Hirose drawing EDC-317849-51-00 rev 1, sheet 3/3, note 10 item (4), viewed; it refers to guideline ETAD-H1015. exports/ldo_b_ldo/parts.csv and exports/ldo_a/parts.csv: J1/J2 at x 91.255 / 108.755; exports/frontend/parts.csv: J1/J2 at x 122.245 / 104.745; both pairs 17.50 mm apart, so the nominal positions agree and the risk is fabrication and placement tolerance. pads.csv on frontend, ldo_a, ldo_b_ldo and ldo_b_router: no pad with drill of 0.8 mm or more. Catalogue p.3: self-alignment +/-0.33 mm. inputs/ldo_a/parts_review_V21/index.html line 68 records the same caution; an earlier ASIC-board review found it on the 80DP drawing EDC3-311351-00. The 70-position drawing itself was not read.
source: Hirose DF40C-120DP-0.4V(51) drawing EDC-317849-51-00 rev 1, sheet 3/3, 'Caution for using multiple connectors'; https://www.hirose.com/en/product/p/CL0684-4107-9-51
consequence: Any position error between J1 and J2 on either board loads the contacts during mating and while seated. With no screws in the head, that stress stays on the contacts.
suggested_action: Ask Hirose (guideline ETAD-H1015) what J1-to-J2 position tolerance they accept, and put that tolerance in the Frontend and LDO-board assembly notes.
v2note: The Frontend and the LDO board are joined by two mated DF40 pairs (J1/J2). Under pin map V6, Option B's J5 would need a second pair as well: it already uses 120 of 120 contacts, V6 adds 12 signals as traced (16 if DISC_OUT is used, and at least 6 even if the far boards' SPI latch and clock and both ports' SPI clock and CLKH are tied on the router), and no DF40 or DF40T part has more than 120 positions, so a DF40 J5 would put two pairs on the joint that is unplugged at every module removal. Hirose's drawing EDC-317849-51-00 rev 1 (sheet 3/3, note 10 (4)) and guideline ETAD-H1015 §1.1.4 say to avoid more than one mated pair between two boards, because the required ±0.01 mm spacing cannot be held, and to use a divided board instead; so before any Option B order the J5 connector has to be chosen (a divided-board DF40 arrangement, one larger connector from another family, or dropping Option B). See LDOB-41. Second check: The facts hold. Router J5 uses all 120 contacts: 108 signals, 3 returns and 9 rails. The V6 trace adds 12 Option B lines, or at least 6 if every router tie is made. Hirose's DF40 catalogue stops at 120 positions. Drawing EDC-317849-51-00 sheet 3/3 note 10(4) says to avoid more than one mated pair. A second pair on J5, which is mated by hand and not fixed down, is riskier than J1/J2. The choice comes before any B order, so major fits. The title must name J5. This duplicates LDOB-41. ETAD ±0.01 mm not verified.

title: Plugging or pulling the B module at J5 pries the router's J3/J4 joints to both ASIC stacks, because nothing else holds the router.
what: The router has no hole or support. It hangs between the two ASIC stacks on J3 (top) and J4 (bottom). The removable module mates to it at J5, whose centre is 6.7 mm from the J3/J4 centre line. Every insertion or withdrawal force at J5 therefore reaches the head through J3 and J4 as a lever load. That load pulls open one contact row of each 80-pin pair, the prying that Hirose warns against. LDOB-06 covers the module's own retention; this adds that every module change also loads, and may partly unmate, the joints to the ASIC stacks on the animal.
where: Router V2. J5 DF40C-120DS (bottom), centre (99.783, 120.2). J3 DF40C-80DP (top), centre (99.783, 113.513), pad rows y 112.158/114.868. J4 DF40C-80DS (bottom), centre (99.783, 113.518), pad rows y 111.978/115.058. No drilled pads.
evidence: exports/ldo_b_router/parts.csv and pads.csv give the positions above; board_stats.txt has Through hole 0 and NPTH 0. The offset is 120.2 - 113.515 = 6.685 mm. A force F at J5 makes a moment of 6.685 x F about the J3/J4 line. With row spacings of 2.71 mm (J3) and 3.08 mm (J4) sharing it, each connector sees about 1.15 x F of row force (6.685 / (2.71 + 3.08)), on top of the direct force. Hirose publishes no DF40 insertion or withdrawal force in the catalogue (also noted in SYS-07), so the absolute load is unknown. No record says how the router or ASIC stacks are held (SYS-07). Merge re-check: the same centres and row spacings in exports/ldo_b_router/parts.csv and pads.csv.
source: Hirose DF40 Series catalogue, 1 Jun 2024 edition: p.21 Precautions (do not support the PCB by the connectors alone; excessive prying when mating or unmating can damage the connector); p.23 Handling Precautions for Connector Removal (do not remove from the width direction); p.5 mating durability 30 times. https://www.hirose.com/en/product/series/DF40. hirose.com returned 403 on 12 Nov 2026, so this was read from the saved copy a review working file (not published) Project records LDOB-06 (known/ldo_b.json) and SYS-07 (known/system.json).
consequence: Module changes can partly unmate or wear the router-to-ASIC-stack joints and their solder joints. These are also 30-cycle parts, on the implanted side, so the result could be intermittent ASIC lanes or rails on the head.
suggested_action: In the LDOB-06 retention decision, require the housing to hold the router itself at J5, not only the module: a backing on the router's top over J5 for insertion and a clamp for withdrawal. Keep that router area free.

title: A V6 Option B that keeps a 1.5 mm DF40 joint needs at least 126 contacts (132 as traced) against the DF40 maximum of 120, so the hand-mated LDO module would join the router through two pairs, which Hirose's DF40C-120DP drawing (sheet 3/3, note 10 (4)) advises against.
what: Hirose's DF40 drawing asks designers to keep one mated pair between two stacked boards. Misalignment between pairs can break connectors during or after mating, and the drawing suggests separate boards for each connection. Today J5 alone joins the router and the LDO board, so it meets this advice (LDOB-28). Under V6 no single connector is big enough, so the removable module must mate through two pairs at once, with no screw or guide, each time it is plugged in on the animal. Pulling two pairs apart in parallel is harder than one. Both router-side halves stay on the head and are rated for 30 cycles.
where: Router-LDO board joint: J5 plus any second pair. The router stays on the head with the four ASIC boards; the LDO board and Frontend are the removable module.
evidence: Hirose drawing EDC-317849-51-00 rev 1, sheet 3/3, note 10 item (4), viewed. The same sheet's un-mating method (1) says parallel un-mating gets harder at high pin counts. DF40 catalogue (2/2024): self-alignment +/-0.33 mm per axis (p.3), 30 mating cycles (p.5), and a precaution not to support the board only by the connectors (p.21). Every option with enough contacts uses two pairs (out/options_table.csv). Neither B board has a mounting hole (LDOB-06).
source: Hirose DF40C-120DP-0.4V(51) drawing EDC-317849-51-00 rev 1, sheet 3/3, 'Caution for using multiple connectors', https://www.hirose.com/en/product/p/CL0684-4107-9-51 (saved copy: a review working file (not published)). Hirose DF40 catalogue 2/2024 pp.3, 5, 21, https://doc.7-el.ru/d/df40.pdf. known/ldo_b.json LDOB-28 and LDOB-06.
consequence: Two pairs on a hand-mated module that comes off every session risk breaking contacts on the router side, which stays on the head with the ASIC boards. Both receptacles wear out together.
suggested_action: Before choosing a two-pair layout, ask Hirose (guideline ETAD-H1015) whether two pairs on a removable module are acceptable and what position tolerance they need between the pairs. If they are not acceptable, drop Option B.

title: Nothing tells the FPGA the ASIC rails are up, so a live mate can drive unpowered ASIC pins, in either option.
what: The ASIC rail regulators on the LDO board are switched on by a local resistor-capacitor delay, their power-good (PG) outputs are unconnected and there is no presence pin, so the Frontend FPGA cannot tell whether the ASIC rails are up. If a connector carrying the 20 FPGA-to-ASIC outputs is mated while the HDMI cable is live, those outputs can drive unpowered ASIC pins and push current into the ASIC's unpowered supplies through its input protection (back-powering). Option A has the identical circuit, so this is not new to Option B: a live J1/J2 mate gives the full delay window in either option, while at Option B's recorded unplug point, J5, the LDO board is already powered and the exposure is only contact order during a rocking mate, with 44 signal pins more than 5 mm from any return contact. The files cannot settle whether this harms the ASIC: that needs the ASIC designer's powered-off and input-clamp limits (ASIC reference item U03) and a recorded rule on whether boards are ever mated live.
where: LDO board (same in Option A): EN_ASIC_RAILS = R1 10 k from VIN_3V3, C3 4.7 uF, TP4, U1 SHDN, U2-U10 EN; PG pins U2.4, U6.4, U8.4, U9.4, U10.4 unconnected; PGFB tied to VIN_3V3 or STIM_PRE. FPGA-driven J5 pins: board clocks 4 and 27, SPI clocks 63 and 64, STIM SPI 20/22/43/45/54/56/58/59, shared controls 61/66/67/69/115/116/117/119. J5 returns: GND 3 and 65, AGND 62. Spare pins J1.29-49 (13 unconnected) on both the LDO board and the Frontend.
evidence: exports/ldo_b_ldo/netlist.xml and pads.csv: EN_ASIC_RAILS reaches no pin of J1, J2 or J5; time constant 10 k x 4.7 uF = 47 ms, roughly 15-22 ms to the enable thresholds (thresholds not checked against the datasheet), then soft start. exports/ldo_a: identical R1/C3 circuit and unconnected PG pins. Twenty FPGA-driven nets from inputs/asic/ASIC_Reference/ASIC_XEM8305_23_Signal_Map.csv directions applied to J5_pin_map_V4.csv (Frontend_V46_pins_V2.xdc sets them to LVCMOS15 but gives no direction). J5 pad distances: 44 signal pins more than 5 mm from a return (26-39 and 88, 90-120), up to 11.13 mm. R2-R5 and R16-R18 (10 k to GND) and R19 (10 k to ASIC_DVDD) hold lines only while the FPGA is not driving. Frontend PUDC_B (U1.J18) is pulled high through R25 470 Ohm, so FPGA I/Os float during configuration and a cold power-up with everything mated is not exposed. exports/hdmi: PORT_ENABLE ties U701-U708 EN together, so one port's power cannot be switched off from the host. Weekly deck record: Option B unplugs the LDO board at J5; Option A assumes the Frontend unplugs from J1/J2. No record states a mating procedure.
source: inputs/asic/ASIC_Reference/ASIC_REFERENCE.md section 10, open item U03 (ASIC powered-off and input-clamp limits absent). LT3042/LT3094 PG, PGFB and EN thresholds: not checked against the datasheet (analog.com fetch timed out). Hirose DF40 hot-plug rating: none found; that DF40 contacts have no make-first length is from memory. Engineering judgement.
consequence: Possible latch-up or damage of the irreplaceable wire-bonded ASICs, or an undefined ASIC state, after a live mate in either option.
suggested_action: Record a 'cable last on, first off' handling rule and ask the ASIC designer for the powered-off input limits. If live mating must be allowed, route a rail-good or presence line to a spare J1 pin on both the LDO board and the Frontend, with a route to an FPGA ball; PG as wired does not report the output rails.
v2note: Under pin map V6 as traced, J3/J4 pins 16, 18, 66, 68, 70 and 72 become FPGA outputs. They carry the far chips' two SPI_DINR/SPI_DINL pairs per port, the top SPI latch and the top SPI clock, so 32 FPGA lines instead of 20 can drive unpowered ASIC inputs on a live mate, and V6's 12 new routes use 12 of the 15 spare Frontend-to-LDO contacts (J1.29-33, 35-37, 39, 43, 45, 47, 49, J2.40, J2.42). Three contacts remain, so a rail-good line (or the EN plus PG pair) still fits and the 'cable last on, first off' rule stays the preferred fix, as already recorded; routing all four near-chip DISC_OUT lines as well would not fit (16 of 15), and tying the top latch and clock to the existing shared latch and per-port SPI clock (the designer's sheet lists both as shared) would reduce the change to 28 lines and 8 contacts.

title: The stimulator pull-downs sit on the removable LDO board, so a module lifted at one end of J5 floats them.
what: In Option B, the only resistors that hold the shared stimulator controls (STIM_EN, STIM_START, STIM_CHB, STIM_CLK) low, and the reset/control pulls R16-R19, are on the plug-in LDO board. The router and the ASIC boards have no pull on these nets. The four STIM contacts are at the east end of J5, while every rail and ground contact is further west, so a module seated at the west end and lifted about 0.5-0.7 mm at the east end keeps all eight ASICs powered while their stimulator inputs float (are connected to nothing). The 120-position DF40 has no lock and neither Option B board has a screw or mounting hole, so an incompletely seated module can stay in this state.
where: Router J5 (DF40C-120DS, bottom, centre 99.783, 120.2): STIM_EN J5.115 and STIM_CHB J5.116 (x 110.783), STIM_CLK J5.117 (x 111.183), STIM_START J5.119 (x 111.583), sharing the last three columns with ASIC5_DATA2 J5.118 and ASIC5_DATA1 J5.120. Rails J5.2/53/55/57/60/70/72/73/75 (x 87.983-102.783), AGND J5.62, GND J5.3/J5.65. LDO board: R2 STIM_EN, R3 STIM_START, R4 STIM_CHB, R5 STIM_CLK (10k to GND); R16 FE_RESET, R17 IMP_TST, R18 SPI_LATCH (10k to GND); R19 CHIP_RESET (10k pull-up to ASIC_DVDD). ASIC board: FPGA_EN, FPGA_START, FPGA_CHBL/R, FPGA_CLK on U01_BCD1/2.
evidence: exports/ldo_b_router/pads.csv and exports/ldo_b_ldo/pads.csv, parts.csv: positions and nets above; router STIM and reset nets touch only J3/J4/J5, and R6 (AC_IN) is the router's only resistor. exports/asic/netlist.xml: no resistor on STIM_EN/START/CLK/CHB, SPI_LATCH, FE_RESET, IMP_TST or CHIP_RESET. Tilt about the west end, contact open when h*(x-87.983)/23.6 > 0.45 mm: rails stay made up to h = 0.45*23.6/14.8 = 0.718 mm; STIM opens above h = 0.45*23.6/22.8 = 0.466 mm; window 1.13-1.74 deg. At h = 0.6 mm, 30 contacts are open (columns 46-60); SPI_LATCH, FE_RESET, IMP_TST and CHIP_RESET stay made. Option A (exports/ldo_a/parts.csv): R2-R5 and R16-R19 are on the same board as J3/J4. ASIC_REFERENCE.md: EN/START/CHB are low at idle; U05 (safe stimulus-disable codes) and U07 (lost-clock behaviour) open. Worst case 8 x 128 x 22.5 uA = 23.0 mA at up to +/-10 V compliance (cells B14-B16).
source: Hirose DF40 Series catalogue: effective mating length 0.45 mm at 1.5 mm stack height; locking design for 10 to 50 positions only; mate and remove in parallel (LCSC copy https://datasheet.lcsc.com/datasheet/pdf/145ab5d527b34eafa7a47375cb561c6a.pdf, page numbers not recovered); DF40C-120DS drawing (mated height 1.5 +/-0.15 mm). ASIC_REFERENCE.md sections 4 and 10 (U05, U07). Engineering judgement: fail-safe pulls belong on the board that stays with the load.
consequence: With a mis-seated or partly lifted module, eight powered stimulators see floating enable, start, charge-balance and clock inputs and nothing on the head holds them off. What the ASIC does in that state is not established, so unintended or DC stimulation current into tissue is possible but not shown.
suggested_action: Move R2-R5, and preferably R16-R19, onto the router beside J3/J4, as R6 already is for AC_IN, before Option B is ordered. Ask the ASIC designer what the stimulator does when powered with EN/START/CLK open.
v2note: LDOB-07 (broader, still major): the STIM pulls R2-R5 and the control pulls R16-R19 sit on the removable LDO board. In addition, the ASIC boards V4 give each port's far board its own latch on connector pin 70 (/T_SPI_LATCH to both top-board chips; pin map V6 ASIC7_8_TOP_SPI_LATCH and ASIC3_4_TOP_SPI_LATCH), and neither any board nor any V6 plan gives these lines a pull, while today's latch SPI_LATCH_SHARED has R18 (10k) on the LDO board. If V6 keeps today's router path (J3.70/J4.70 to J5.90/J5.89 at x 105.583, east of the last rail contact at x 102.783), those J5 contacts open at a 0.603 mm lift while the rails stay made up to 0.718 mm, so their 10k pull-downs belong on the router with R2-R5, not beside R18 on the LDO board. See LDOA-56.

title: Nothing on the head protects ASIC pins at router J5 from static discharge, and no mating procedure exists.
what: ESD (electrostatic discharge) is the spark of static charge from a hand, tool or module into a pin. All 108 J5 signal contacts run through plain copper on the router to the ASIC boards with no series resistor, clamp diode, TVS (transient voltage suppressor) or make-first ground contact. With the module off, the router and ASIC boards float, tied to the animal only through the ASIC dies and AGND, so whichever J5 contact touches first takes the discharge. The ASIC's ESD rating is not recorded, and no handling procedure or exposed ground touch pad exists; whether to add one is a decision to make before ordering.
where: Router (ldo_b_router) J5 DF40C-120DS, bottom: 108 signal contacts; rails J5.2/53/55/57/60/70/72/73/75; GND J5.3/J5.65; AGND J5.62 -> router J3/J4.42/44 -> ASIC board J1 (one-pin 1 mm header on /AGND). Router GND (L3) and AGND (L4) are separate; the only tie, NT1, is on the LDO board. Frontend side: U701-U708 EN all on PORT_ENABLE (HDMI Extension Board).
evidence: exports/ldo_b_router/parts.csv: only C51, C53-C57 (1 uF, rail to AGND), R6, TP7, J3, J4, J5; J5 metal-fitting pads have no net. Each of the 108 J5 signal nets reaches only router J3/J4. exports/asic/parts.csv: only capacitors, J1, J3, J4, U01_BCD1/2; J1.1 = /AGND. Of the 108 signals, 64 land on U01_BCD1/2 pads of the existing ASIC board; 44 are T_ pass-through nets for the second ASIC board, which has no CAD (inputs/asic/J3_pinout__J3_Pinout.csv: pass-through, no chip connection). VDD10, VSS10 and VDD_ADC have no router capacitor but have C18/C19, C25/C26 and C1/C34 on the ASIC board. ASIC_REFERENCE.md line 175 (U03): absolute, input-clamp and powered-off limits absent; no ESD/HBM text. Human-body-model scale: 100 pF x 2 kV = 200 nC, 2 kV / 1.5 kohm = 1.33 A peak, about 8.9 x the 22.5 nC largest stimulus phase; 200 nC on 1 uF raises a rail 0.2 V. inputs/notes/fpga-ldo-v14.md: router stays on the head, module plugs in from above.
source: ASIC_REFERENCE.md U03 (inputs/asic/ASIC_Reference). Hirose DF40 catalogue 2013.11, p.1 features (no make-first contacts on DF40C; ground contacts only on DF40GB shielded types). Human-body-model network 100 pF / 1.5 kohm (JEDEC JS-001, from memory, not re-checked). Engineering judgement.
consequence: Each mating risks an ESD hit to an ASIC on an implanted probe, which cannot be replaced without surgery, and may drive a short current pulse through the electrodes. Nothing in the files says J1 is a tissue reference electrode, so the tissue path is inferred.
suggested_action: Decide and write the mating procedure (handler and module bonded to the head's ground before J5 touches), and decide whether to add a bare GND/AGND touch pad on the router edge. Get the ASIC pad ESD rating from the ASIC designer.
v2note: Nothing on the head protects the ASIC pins from static discharge, either at router J5 or at the open DF40 end of each far ASIC board. With ASIC V4, all 108 J5 signal contacts end on chip pads, 44 of them on the far chips. Both V4 boards fit J3 and J4 (J3.n = J4.n on 80/80 pins), so each port's far board leaves its J4 plug (J3 port) or J3 receptacle (J4 port) open. That open end has 67 signal contacts: 9 to all four chips, 30 to the near chips only and 28 to the far chips only. It also has +10 V and -10 V on pins 36 and 54, and no series part or clamp. These open ends exist in Option A as well, and whether or not the LDO module is fitted, so a J5 mating procedure and a router touch pad do not cover them. A cover or a one-connector variant per port, a handling procedure for the whole head and the ASIC pad ESD rating must be settled before ordering. This overlaps the pair-stacking free-end item and R2S-10, which treat the open end only as a short-circuit and cover question. See SYS-55.

title: With the likely 0.1-0.22 uF ASIC-board capacitors (values not yet chosen), a live J5 mate rings VDD10 and VSS10 at the ASIC boards to about +10.5 to +12 V and -12 to -14 V typical, and up to about +16/-17 V, past their ±10 V setting.
what: When J5 closes with the HDMI cable live, the charged 22 uF (VDD10) and 32 uF (VSS10) output capacitors on the LDO board discharge into the empty capacitors on the four ASIC boards through roughly 6-18 nH of copper and contacts. Each ASIC board has only two 0201 capacitors on each +/-10 V rail and the router has none, so the loop is underdamped and the ASIC-side voltage overshoots before it settles. This is the ringing that ADI's AN88 describes for hot-plugged ceramic capacitors (up to twice the step). The overshoot reaches the stimulator supply of all eight ASICs, and no ASIC supply limit is on record.
where: LDO board U9/C902 (ASIC_VDD10, J5.55, x 98.783) and U10/C1002+C1004 (ASIC_VSS10, J5.73, x 102.383); router J5 to J3/J4 pins 36/54 (3.6 mm of 0.2 mm L6, no capacitor); ASIC boards C18/C19 (VDD10) and C25/C26 (VSS10), 0201, value 'C_Small_US', on all four boards.
evidence: Lumped model per rail (a review working file (not published), sim.py; results flat_rows.json, rock_out.txt): source 9.9 uF (VDD10) and 13.9 uF (VSS10) effective at 10 V; head 8 parts; loop R 52/110/242 mOhm plus the shared J5.62 return 12/35/100 mOhm; L 5.6/9.3/15 nH plus 0.8-3 nH (copper from board.json: C902 to J5 11.5 mm, C1002 to J5 15.6 mm of 0.2 mm L6; router 3.6 mm). ASIC-side peak with 0.1 uF parts: VDD10 12.0 V typical (10.0-15.3 V over the R/L corners), VSS10 -13.7 V (-11.5 to -17.2 V); 0.22 uF parts: 10.5 V (9.9-14.0) and -12.0 V (-10.2 to -15.8); 1 uF parts: 8.5-10.7 V and -9.5 to -12.1 V; 4.7 uF parts: no overshoot but a step to about +/-6-7.5 V. A +/-10 V rail making alone in a rocking mate gives the same (VDD10 12.0 V typical, up to 15.8 V). Ringing lasts about 0.1-0.5 us. A 0.47 ohm series resistor in each +/-10 V rail keeps the head at or below 10.07 V in every corner (damp_test_out.txt, mono_out.txt), costing 8 mV at the 8 mA budget maximum. The LDO side stays inside the LT3042/LT3094 ratings (source dips to 4.9-9.6 V). Only about 0.1-0.22 uF 0201 parts rated 16 V or more exist (from memory), so the small-capacitor case is the likely one.
source: ADI Application Note 88, 'Ceramic Input Capacitors Can Cause Overvoltage Transients' (G. Perica), read as reprinted at https://www.radiolocman.com/review/article.html?di=665593 (Tables 1 and 3, Figures 2-4); the original https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/application-notes/an88f.pdf timed out three times. Project files: exports/ldo_b_ldo/netlist.xml, exports/ldo_b_router/netlist.xml, exports/asic_top/netlist.xml, exports/asic_bottom/netlist.xml and each board.json. inputs/asic/ASIC_Reference/ASIC_REFERENCE.md lines 174-175 (U02, U03); known SYS-45 (no ASIC supply absolute maximum).
consequence: Every live mate can put a 20-70 % overvoltage spike on the stimulator supply of all eight ASICs; whether they survive cannot be judged until the ASIC limits are known.
suggested_action: Keep live mating out by rule (next finding). As cheap insurance, add a 0.47-1 ohm resistor in series with ASIC_VDD10 and ASIC_VSS10 on the LDO board between C902/C1002 and J5, and ask the ASIC designer for the VDD10/VSS10 absolute maximum.

title: In any live J5 mate that is not perfectly parallel, rails whose head capacitors return to AGND connect together with a GND contact before J5.62, the only AGND contact, so their charging current must pass through the ASIC dies' undocumented AGND-DGND link; this is about 18-600 uC nominal when the mate starts at the west end.
what: LDOB-24 examined a module resting on its east end with every return open. Starting from the west end is just as likely and is different: VDD_CGEN makes before any ground, GND J5.3 makes next, and VDD10, VDD_DRIVER and REF_VCM make while J5.62 is still open. Their head capacitors return only to AGND, and on the router and ASIC boards AGND meets DGND nowhere except inside the dies. So the charge must flow through the dies' unknown AGND-DGND link, or the analogue domain is pushed up to about 10 V above DGND, until J5.62 makes and takes the released surge of four rails at once. This happens briefly in any live mate that is not parallel, not only when a module is left tilted.
where: J5.2 VDD_CGEN (x 87.983), J5.3 GND (88.383), J5.53 DVDD (98.383), J5.55 VDD10 (98.783), J5.57 VDD_DRIVER (99.183), J5.60 REF_VCM (99.583), J5.62 AGND (99.983). Router GND (L3) and AGND (L4) separate; ASIC /AGND (J3/J4 42, 44) and /DGND (46, 48) joined only by J3, J4 and U01_BCD1/2.
evidence: exports/ldo_b_router/pads.csv x positions. Netlist check on asic_top, asic_bottom and ldo_b_router: the only parts touching both AGND and DGND/GND are J3, J4, J5 and the two dies. Head capacitors on /AGND: VDD10 C18/C19, VDD_DRIVER C41/C42/C59/C60, REF_VCM C5/C46/C57/C58, VDD_CGEN C6/C50, router C51-C57. Charge to move: VDD10 3.6-75 uC, VDD_DRIVER 3.5-58 uC, REF_VCM 1.9-37 uC, VDD_CGEN 2.4-29 uC (0.1-4.7 uF parts). Release through J5.62 when it makes: 32-49 A typical, up to 102 A. East end first: VDD_ADC/VSS10/REF_VDD/VDD_FE make before any return (as LDOB-24); J5.62 release 13-54 A, then VDD10 alone 34-107 A (rock_out.txt, rock_rows.json).
source: inputs/asic/ASIC_Reference/ASIC_REFERENCE.md line 176 (U04: actual AGND/DGND bond unknown); Hirose DF40 catalogue (Feb 2024) pp.22-23 (mate and remove parallel), LCSC copy https://datasheet.lcsc.com/datasheet/pdf/145ab5d527b34eafa7a47375cb561c6a.pdf?productCode=C3640153; known LDOB-24 and LDOB-02.
consequence: Any non-parallel live mate, from either end, drives rail-charging current through the ASIC dies' ground structures or lifts the analogue domain by up to 10 V relative to DGND for as long as the rocking takes.
suggested_action: Covered by the cable-off rule. In the J5 re-pin planned under LDOB-01/LDOB-24 and pin map V6, make the end-column and rail-adjacent returns AGND, including beside J5.55 and J5.73; a GND contact does not serve these eight rails.

title: Each ASIC rail crosses the removable J5 on a single contact, so one worn or dirty contact drops that rail on all eight ASICs.
what: Option B sends each of the nine ASIC rails through exactly one J5 contact and then splits it to both ASIC stacks on the router. J5 is the joint unplugged whenever the module comes off (how often is not recorded, LDOB-06), is rated for 30 cycles, and stays open on the head between sessions (LDOB-22). If one rail contact goes high-resistance or open, that rail disappears from all eight ASICs while the other rails and the FPGA-driven lines stay live. Nothing reports this (LDOB-04). In Option A each rail reaches each stack on its own contact, on connectors that are mated once.
where: J5 on both B boards: VDD_CGEN pin 2, DVDD 53, VDD10 55, VDD_DRIVER 57, REF_VCM 60, VDD_FE 70, REF_VDD 72, VSS10 73, VDD_ADC 75. The router fans these out to J3/J4 pins 1, 34, 36, 38, 40, 50, 52, 54 and 56.
evidence: inputs/ldo_b/V2_record/J5_pin_map_V4.csv and exports/ldo_b_router/netlist.xml: each /ASIC_* rail net is one J5 pad plus J3.n and J4.n (plus one router capacitor on six rails). Hirose: 30 mating cycles, 90 mOhm maximum afterwards. The ASIC's behaviour with one rail missing is not documented (ASIC_REFERENCE open items U02/U03). The rail currents are mA-level, so this is about losing the contact, not about current rating. Merge re-check: exports/ldo_b_router/netlist.xml gives each of the nine /ASIC_* rail nets exactly one J5 pad. Known context: LDOB-02 already calls the single AGND contact J5.62 a single point of failure, and LDOB-29 counts one contact per rail only for current; neither covers losing a rail contact.
source: Hirose DF40 catalogue, 1 Jun 2024, p.5 (mating durability, contact resistance), https://www.hirose.com/en/product/series/DF40 (saved copy a review working file (not published); hirose.com returned 403); engineering judgement (redundant contacts on a frequently mated power interface). Project records LDOB-02, LDOB-04, LDOB-22 and LDOB-29 (known/ldo_b.json).
consequence: All eight ASICs could be powered with one rail missing while the rest and their inputs are live. The effect on the ASIC is unknown.
suggested_action: When J5 is re-planned (needed anyway for pin map V6 and LDOB-01), give each rail two non-adjacent contacts. Until then, add a rail check at each session start-up.

title: Five LDO-board regulators reach their ground plane only through 10-18 mm of thin bottom-layer track.
what: U2, U6 and U8 have vias in their exposed (thermal) pads that reach the ground planes in 0.63 mm. The north-row regulators U3, U4, U5, U9 and U10 do not: their grounds run through 10-18 mm of 0.12-0.30 mm L6 track to two microvia plus buried-via chains before reaching the L2 AGND plane (U3 reaches the GND planes the same way). For the +10 V (U9, LT3042) and -10 V (U10, LT3094) regulators, the ground of the SET resistor, which sets the output voltage, is 11-14 mm of copper from the regulator's own ground, so ground current along that track adds into the reference. Loads are a few mA, so this is a noise issue, not a failure.
where: LDO board underside L6: U9 (95.4, 132.15) VDD10, U10 (107.55, 132.15) VSS10, U4 VDD_DRIVER, U5 DVDD, U3 VDD_ADC (GND net); R901, C903, R1001, C1003. Plane entries: microvia (93.15, 136.41) + buried via (92.9, 137.11) and microvia (106.45, 136.06) + buried via (106.25, 137.11).
evidence: Shortest copper path to a plane-reaching via (a review working file (not published) on exports/ldo_b_ldo/board.json): U9.11 EP 18.43 mm; U10.9 17.48 mm; U4 17.95-18.49 mm; U5.5 10.33 mm; U3.5 (GND) 12.84 mm; NT1.2 17.22 mm; U2/U6/U8 pad 11 0.63 mm. Pad-to-pad ground path: U9.11-R901.2 13.90 mm, U9.11-C903.2 12.55 mm, U10.9-R1001.2 11.14 mm, U10.9-C1003.2 9.79 mm, U10.9-C1001.2 15.72 mm. AGND L6 track widths 0.12-0.30 mm; all 12 AGND through vias are in the south and middle rows.
source: TI TPS7A20 SBVS338H (Jul 2024), section 7.4.1, p31 (place capacitors close, use copper planes, no via directly under the DQN thermal pad), https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tps7a20.pdf ; LT3042 / LT3094 layout guidance not checked against the datasheet (analog.com unreachable), so the SET-ground point is engineering judgement.
consequence: Extra ground impedance and shared ground current in the SET reference of the +/-10 V stimulation rails and in the returns of three ASIC rails; a likely source of low-level noise.
suggested_action: Add an AGND via (L6 to L2) beside each north-row regulator's ground pad (not under a TPS7A20 thermal pad) and at the R901/C903 and R1001/C1003 ground pads where the lane field allows.

title: All of the B LDO board's 3.3 V input current passes through one 0.15 mm through via, as on Option A.
what: VIN_3V3 enters on J2.68-70 on the top layer. It reaches the bottom-layer pour that feeds every regulator and the LT3582 through a single through via. Removing that via in a copy of the board cuts J2.68-70 off from all 27 other VIN_3V3 pads. LDOA-18 found the same on Option A, but it is not on the B list. The via's capacity is not the problem; the lack of a second path is.
evidence: a review working file (not published) (pcbnew connectivity on a read-only load): normally J2.68 reaches all 30 VIN_3V3 pads. With via (109.0, 140.81) removed it reaches only J2.68-70; C1, C2, C11, C201-C801, L11, R1, TP1, U1.5 and the U2-U8 inputs become unreachable. The other L1-L6 VIN via (93.725, 145.96) only joins TP1's L1 piece to L11.1. Expected current is about 167 mA (LDOA-18). The merge repeated the test on a hash-identical copy of the board (a review working file (not published)): 30 of 30 pads with the via, J2.68-70 only (3 of 30) without.
source: Engineering judgement; project record known/ldo_a.json LDOA-18 (same via at (109.00, 135.00) on Option A V12).
consequence: One defective plated hole would leave every ASIC rail and the +/-12 V converter unpowered. There is no current or noise problem otherwise.
suggested_action: Add at least two more through vias between the J2 VIN_3V3 L1 piece and the L6 pour, as proposed for LDOA-18.

title: Three router clock lanes run 10-15 mm at a 0.10 mm gap between two switching lines, below good practice.
what: Crosstalk is noise coupled from a switching line into its neighbour. On the router, the ASIC1 and ASIC5 32 MHz clocks and STIM_CLK each run with a switching line 0.10 mm away on both sides, while their ground plane is two layers down (about 0.30 mm, assuming Option A's JLC stack because the router file has no stack-up). Good practice keeps a clock at least 2-3 dielectric heights from switching lines; here the gap is about one third of a height. Modelled noise stays below the FPGA's input margin in every case, and the ASIC launches its data near the clock's rising edge, so this eats margin rather than causing a likely failure; the real risk is only together with the J5 return-bounce finding.
where: Router L1 ASIC5_CLK32MHz_Out (J3.45 to J5.112) between ASIC5_DATA5 and ASIC5_SYNC, y 113.21 x 100.98-109.18 and x 109.38 y 113.41-120.6. Router L6 ASIC1_CLK32MHz_Out (J4.45 to J5.111) between ASIC1_DATA5 and ASIC1_SYNC, y 113.38 x 100.98-108.78. Router L6 STIM_CLK_SHARED between STIM_EN_SHARED and STIM_START_SHARED, y 112.78 x 102.58-109.38. Shorter runs: ASIC4 CLK32 (L6, 3.6 mm), BOARD1_SPI_CLK (L5, 3.2 mm), BOARD3_SPI_CLK (L2, 2.8 mm).
evidence: exports/ldo_b_router/board.json scanned by both checkers, 0.10 mm tracks at 0.10 mm edge gap: ASIC5 CLK32 14.99/14.79 mm of 18.37 mm; ASIC1 11.02/10.82 of 15.06 mm; STIM_CLK 10.02/9.82 of 14.36 mm. exports/ldo_b_router/zones.csv: no pour on L2 or L5; L3 GND and L4 AGND. stackup.txt empty; plane height 0.071 + 0.03 + 0.201 = 0.302 mm from inputs/ldo_a/V12_checks/JLC_stackup_JLCH061611Y1-1078.json (assumed). Backward coupling per neighbour about 0.18-0.20 at 0.10 mm gap, about 0.08-0.09 at 0.30 mm (two independent 2-D solves). Peak noise on a quiet clock, both neighbours switching: original model 0.24/0.33 V (ASIC5, 25 ohm source, 1/0.5 ns edges); checker's router-only model 81-121 mV at 1 ns and 281-406 mV at 0.5 ns. All below the 0.525 V LVCMOS15 margin (VIL = 35 % of 1.5 V). The edge sweep stays monotonic. STIM_CLK goes to the ASIC, whose thresholds are unknown (ASIC_REFERENCE.md U03), so that margin applies only to the CLK32 lanes.
source: AMD DS181 v1.27.1, Table 8 p.9 (LVCMOS15 VIL/VIH), https://docs.amd.com/v/u/en-US/ds181_Artix_7_Data_Sheet (404 today; values from a saved copy); JLC template JLCH061611Y1-1078; ASIC_REFERENCE.md U03 and logic_primary_findings.md line 70; engineering judgement (2-3 dielectric heights to switching lines).
consequence: The clock lanes keep less noise margin than they should; combined with J5 return bounce this could produce a false clock edge. Option B has no order files yet, so a fix costs no board spin.
suggested_action: On the router, widen the gaps on both sides of these clock lanes to at least 0.3 mm, or add a GND guard on L1/L6 stitched to L3/L4, then re-run the scan.

title: On the LDO board, L2 signal lanes cut the AGND plane under the L1 CLK32 clocks of ASIC7 and ASIC5.
what: A trace on L1 uses the solid AGND plane on L2, 0.071 mm below, as its reference: its return current flows in that plane right under it. Where L2 carries its own signal lanes the plane is cut, so the L1 clock above loses that close reference and sees L3, 0.30 mm away, instead. Over about 4.8 mm of the ASIC7 CLK32 clock and about 2.1 mm of the ASIC5 CLK32 clock there is no AGND beneath, and in places each clock lies directly over an L2 signal lane. ASIC7's clock keeps 0.10 mm neighbours in that stretch, so its coupling to them rises to about the router's L1 level; ASIC5's neighbours there are about 0.3 mm away, so its increase is smaller.
where: LDO board V2, L1. ASIC7_CLK32MHz_Out: x 105.85, y 127.36-130.50 (3.15 mm) and along y 130.81, x 106.16-107.40 plus the 45 degree piece (1.67 mm). ASIC5_CLK32MHz_Out: along y 128.01, x 107.41-108.70 (1.30 mm) and at x 108.7-109.0 (0.77 mm). L2 lanes beneath: ASIC3_DATA8 under ASIC7 CLK32 for 1.39 mm, ASIC5_DATA4 under ASIC5 CLK32 for 1.44 mm. Neighbours in the ASIC7 void: ASIC7_DATA5 and ASIC7_SYNC at 0.10 mm.
evidence: Zones refilled with pcbnew on a scratch copy of boards/ldo_b_ldo, L1 clock centrelines sampled against the filled L2 (In1.Cu) AGND polygons: ASIC7 CLK32 has 4.83 mm of its 10.74 mm L1 length with no AGND beneath; ASIC5 CLK32 has 2.07 mm of 8.29 mm (the first pass measured 4.14 and 1.82 mm). Neighbours inside the ASIC7 void: DATA5 0.10 mm for 3.16 mm, SYNC 0.10 mm for 2.89 mm; inside the ASIC5 void: DATA5 0.30 mm, GND 0.28 mm. Stack from inputs/ldo_a/V12_checks/JLC_stackup_JLCH061611Y1-1078.json: L1-L2 0.071 mm, L2-L3 0.201 mm. Treating 2.5 mm of ASIC7 CLK32 with the 0.30 mm-height coupling (Kb 0.193 instead of 0.087) raised its crosstalk at the FPGA from 132 to 175 mV (0.5 ns edge, 25 ohm); the re-check's short-line estimate (a few tens of mV more) agrees in size but did not re-run that model.
source: Engineering judgement; JLC stack-up template JLCH061611Y1-1078 layer heights.
consequence: Extra crosstalk and a break in the return path on two clocks. Small alone, it adds to the J5 return and router lane-crosstalk problems on the CLK32 clocks.
suggested_action: Move the L2 lanes out from under these two L1 clocks, or shift the clocks' L1 runs sideways onto solid AGND.

title: On the LDO board, L5 clock lanes keep switching reference between L4 GND and L6 rail pours along their length.
what: L5 sits 0.201 mm below the L4 GND plane but only 0.071 mm above L6, which is a patchwork of power-rail pours. Where a rail pour lies under a lane, that rail is the nearer plane and carries most of the lane's return current, which then has to cross to GND through decoupling capacitors. The clock lanes change reference 7 to 12 times, and the trace impedance steps between about 40 ohm (over a pour) and 70 ohm (without one), causing small reflections at each step.
where: LDO board V2, L5 over L6. ASIC1_CLK32MHz_Out (x 108.62, y 122.8-137.6): under STIM_PRE_NEG 5.5 mm, ASIC_VSS10 3.3 mm, ASIC_VDD_ADC 1.8 mm. STIM_CLK_SHARED: under VIN_3V3 7.2 mm, ASIC_VDD_ADC 5.0 mm. ASIC2_CLK32MHz_Out: under ASIC_VDD10 4.2 mm, STIM_PRE_POS 3.7 mm. BOARD1_SPI_CLK: under ASIC_VDD_DRIVER 3.2 mm.
evidence: Re-check on pcbnew-refilled L6 pours (lengths agree within 0.05 mm with the first pass). ASIC1 CLK32: L5 length 19.18 mm; STIM_PRE_NEG 5.53, VSS10 3.27, VDD_ADC 1.80, VIN_3V3 0.55 mm; no L6 copper 8.03 mm; 8 changes. ASIC2: VDD10 4.22, STIM_PRE_POS 3.68, VIN_3V3 1.29, DVDD 1.0 mm. STIM_CLK: VIN_3V3 7.17, VDD_ADC 4.96 mm. BOARD1_SPI_CLK: VDD_DRIVER 3.16 mm, plus 1.87 mm under an AGND track. L4 GND is missing for only about 1 mm per lane, near the connector ends. Impedance: field solve 43 ohm under a pour and 72 ohm without; hand estimate (w 0.1 mm, t 0.03 mm, 0.071 / 0.201 mm, Dk about 4.2) about 40 and 70 ohm. Coupling at 0.25 mm gap: Kb 0.013 under a pour, 0.089 without. Stack from inputs/ldo_a/V12_checks/JLC_stackup_JLCH061611Y1-1078.json. The first pass's LDO-board crosstalk shares (ASIC4 CLK32 133 mV, BOARD1_CLK 134-144 mV, BOARD1_SPI_CLK 110 mV, ASIC1 CLK32 72 mV, STIM_CLK 62 mV at 0.5 ns, 25 ohm) were not re-run.
source: Engineering judgement; JLC stack-up template JLCH061611Y1-1078 layer heights.
consequence: Reflections at each change of reference, and clock return current flowing in the stimulation and 3.3 V rails. This adds to the J5 return problem rather than failing on its own.
suggested_action: Keep L6 clear under the L5 clock lanes, or fill that area with stitched GND. Otherwise add GND stitching vias beside the lanes where they pass over rail pours.

title: The CLKH clock to the lower ASIC pair runs 11 mm beside two ASIC outputs whose crosstalk lands at its input.
what: BOARD1_CLK carries CLKH, the FPGA's 32 MHz clock, to the lower ASIC pair. On the LDO board it runs between ASIC4_DATA1 and ASIC2_READ, both driven from the ASIC end. Near-end (backward) crosstalk from a line driven at the far end appears at the ASIC end, which is the clock's receiver, and the unterminated input doubles it there. The files cannot settle whether this matters, because the ASIC's input thresholds and hysteresis are not documented; the ASIC designer's figures for them would.
where: LDO board V2: BOARD1_CLK on L5 (x 94.18, y 122.45-134.01), 0.25 mm from ASIC4_DATA1 (11.6 mm) and ASIC2_READ (11.2 mm); on L2 (y 134.01, x 89.9-94.18), 0.30 mm from both for about 4 mm. Router V2 L5: 0.30 mm from ASIC2_READ for 6.46 mm. Router J4.7 and J5.27 = BOARD1_CLK; ASIC connector pin 7 = CLKH.
evidence: Track dump of the refilled LDO and router boards: LDO L5 neighbours ASIC4_DATA1 0.25 mm for 11.58 mm, ASIC2_READ 0.25 mm for 11.15 mm; L2 both at 0.30 mm for 4.0-4.3 mm; router L5 ASIC2_READ 0.30 mm for 6.46 mm. exports/ldo_b_router/pads.csv: J4.7 and J5.27 = /BOARD1_CLK; inputs/asic/J3_pinout__J3_Pinout.csv pin 7 = CLKH. Time-domain peak at the ASIC end, both neighbours switching, 25 ohm: +99/-115 mV at 1 ns edges, +163/-177 mV at 0.5 ns, of which the LDO board contributes 134-144 mV; the ASIC-board part of the path is not included. Re-check short-line estimate (Kb 0.089, 2TD about 145 ps, 0.5 ns edge, doubled, two neighbours): about 150 mV plus the router part.
source: ASIC_REFERENCE.md section 3 (controller supplies CLKH) and U03 (ASIC VIH/VIL not given); engineering judgement.
consequence: If the ASIC clock input has a narrow margin or no hysteresis, READ and DATA activity could add false edges to CLKH and shift the ASIC's frame counting.
suggested_action: Ask the ASIC designer for the input thresholds and hysteresis of CLKH, SPI_CLK and STIM_CLK. If none are available, open the gap around BOARD1_CLK on LDO-board L5 to 0.5 mm.

title: Under V6, 18 existing J5 contacts change role, so LDOB-09, -23, -25, -26 and -32 must be redone; LDOB-27 still holds.
what: Renaming lines to V6 changes what 18 existing J5 contacts carry. Twelve reverse direction and become FPGA outputs: 8 SPI data lines, 2 top-chip latches and 2 top-chip SPI clocks. Four former data contacts become returned 32 MHz clocks, and two former clock contacts become data. The J5 clock-noise model (LDOB-09) assumed the old clock positions and 80 ASIC outputs switching. Under V6, four clocks move and 88 ASIC outputs plus 32 FPGA outputs switch. If the lanes are reused as traced, two new clock-beside-data runs appear on the LDO board, on L1. The new ASIC7 clock runs about 9 mm at a 0.10 mm gap between two ASIC7 outputs. The new top-chip SPI clock runs 7.4 mm at 0.10 mm beside an ASIC7 output.
where: J5.11, 13, 38, 40, 85-88: data to SPI data out. J5.7, 34, 81, 82: data to CLK32 of ASIC4, 8, 3 and 7. J5.15, 42: CLK32 to data. J5.89, 90: CLK32 to top latch. J5.91, 92: SYNC to top SPI clock. LDO board L1: the old ASIC7_DATA8 and ASIC7_SYNC lanes.
evidence: out/v6_j5_existing_contacts.csv, made by joining the V6 trace to J5_pin_map_V4.csv through router_target. Nearest return pad on the router: ASIC4 clock 2.4 -> 0.8 mm, ASIC8 4.0 -> 5.6 mm, ASIC3 4.8 -> 3.2 mm, ASIC7 5.6 -> 4.0 mm. Lane scan at a 0.10 mm edge gap (out/step1_lane_neighbours.txt): on the LDO board, the old ASIC7_DATA8 lane runs 8.99 / 8.39 mm beside two ASIC7 outputs. The old ASIC7_SYNC lane runs 7.59 mm beside the new latch and 7.39 mm beside ASIC7_DATA4. On the router, the old ASIC4_DATA8 lane runs 3.65 mm beside two outputs. The router ASIC1/ASIC5 clock runs are unchanged (11.1 / 15.1 mm, as in LDOB-23). BOARD1_CLK's neighbours (LDOB-27) stay ASIC outputs. If the clock-ball fix is made on the router, the eight clocks keep their LDOB-09 contacts.
source: known/pinmap_v6_trace.csv; inputs/ldo_b/V2_record/J5_pin_map_V4.csv; exports/ldo_b_router/board.json; exports/ldo_b_ldo/board.json; known/ldo_b.json LDOB-09, -23, -25, -26, -27, -32; engineering judgement.
consequence: The current J5 signal-integrity conclusions do not describe a V6 Option B. Reusing the lanes as traced adds clock-beside-data runs of the kind LDOB-23 already flags.
suggested_action: Treat LDOB-09, -23, -25, -26 and -32 as open again for any V6 Option B and redo them on the new J5 map. Carry LDOB-27 over with the new names.

title: Both Option B boards have rule files KiCad ignores, silkscreen below JLC limits and empty title blocks.
what: A .kicad_dru file holds extra design rules for KiCad's rule check (DRC). In both B rule files the limits have no units, so KiCad applies nothing, and both files lack the JLC hole, edge and silkscreen rules that Option A V12 added. Both boards keep 0.12 mm silkscreen lines and 0.6-0.8 mm text, below JLC's 0.15 mm and 1.0 mm minimums, both PCB title blocks are empty, and comment 1 of both schematic title blocks still says 'Schematic only, no layout'. The copper itself passes the intended ring limits once units are added, and no Gerber, drill, BOM or placement files exist yet.
