where: boards/ldo_b_router/FPGA_LDO_B_Router_Layout_V2.kicad_dru and boards/ldo_b_ldo/FPGA_LDO_B_LDO_Layout_V2.kicad_dru ('(min 0.075)', '(min 0.1)'); F.SilkS/B.SilkS on both boards; title_block of both .kicad_pcb files; schematic title-block comment 1 on both boards.
evidence: Scratch DRC on the router (kicad-cli 10.0.6): 'annular_width (min 0.2)' gives 0 violations, '(min 0.2mm)' gives 149. Original rules with units added: 0 violations on both boards. Silk census (pcbnew): router 42 lines at 0.12 mm, 5 texts 0.6 mm high; LDO board 206 lines at 0.12 mm, 32 texts 0.6-0.8 mm high. Both .kicad_pro: min_text_height 0.6, min_silk_clearance 0. DRC with Option A V12's rule file: router 29 silk_over_copper, 5 text_height, 5 text_thickness; LDO board 129 silk_over_copper, 32 text_height, 2 text_thickness; no copper or hole errors. Neither .kicad_pcb has a title_block (summary.txt title ''). LDO schematic comment 2 (3x LT3042 for ASIC rails plus an LT3042/LT3094 pair) matches U2/U6/U8/U9 and U10 and is correct. No Gerber, drill, BOM or placement files under inputs/ldo_b.
source: JLCPCB PCB capabilities (legend line >= 0.15 mm, text >= 1.0 mm), https://jlcpcb.com/capabilities/pcb-capabilities ; JLCPCB HDI capabilities as cited in Option A's .kicad_dru, https://jlcpcb.com/help/article/hdi-pcb-capabilities-faq ; inputs/ldo_a/V12_record/START_HERE.md (same defects fixed in Option A V12).
consequence: Later edits can break JLC limits without DRC noticing, small legend text may be dropped or smeared at the factory, and the stale notes mislead at bring-up.
suggested_action: Copy Option A V12's rule file and silkscreen clean-up to both B boards, fill the title blocks and correct comment 1, then rerun DRC before making order files.

title: The J5 pads get a full-size paste opening; Hirose asks for 80 % and a flat board under the connector.
what: The stencil is the thin metal sheet that prints solder paste onto the pads; its openings set how much paste each pad gets. Hirose asks for a 0.12 mm stencil with openings at 80 % of the pad, a board that bows no more than 0.02 mm at the connector centre, and at most two reflow passes. Both B boards print paste over the whole pad (100 %), and nothing in the B files states the flatness limit. J5 is the longest connector in the system, so board bow matters most here.
where: Router J5 (DF40C-120DS, bottom) and LDO board J5 (DF40C-120DP, top); the same settings apply to router J3/J4 and LDO board J1/J2.
evidence: pcbnew on boards/ldo_b_router/FPGA_LDO_B_Router_Layout_V2.kicad_pcb and boards/ldo_b_ldo/FPGA_LDO_B_LDO_Layout_V2.kicad_pcb: board paste margin 0, ratio 0; no pad or footprint paste override on any J pad. exports/ldo_b_*/summary.txt: paste_margin 0.0. Pad gaps: LDO board J5 pads 0.23 x 0.66 mm at 0.4 mm pitch leave 0.17 mm; router J5 pads 0.20 x 0.70 mm leave 0.20 mm. The router already needs both allowed reflows (J3 on top; J4 and J5 on the bottom). No B order files exist yet.
source: Hirose DF40 catalogue (Aug 1 2022), p.16 Operating Precautions 1-4 (0.12 mm stencil, 80 % opening on DS and DP, board lean max 0.02 mm at connector centre, 2 reflow cycles max); the Jun 2024 catalogue p.21 says the same.
consequence: Too much paste can bridge neighbouring pads, and a bowed board can leave open joints at the connector centre.
suggested_action: Set an 80 % paste opening on the DF40 pads (or ask JLC for it) and state the 0.02 mm flatness and two-reflow limits in the B order note.

title: Most Option B parts, including both J5 halves, have no LCSC number, so no JLC order can be built yet.
what: JLC assembly needs an LCSC part number on every line of the parts list (BOM). Both J5 halves do have JLC parts (plug C22426477, receptacle C3647197, both Extended library), but neither number is in the B schematics, and only 5 of the 75 LDO-board parts and none of the 11 router parts carry an LCSC number. The B LDO board also uses the same parts that are out of stock or unchosen in Option A (U1, D11, D12, L11, L12), and the B record does not list them. Neither JLC part page showed a J5 stock count, so stock must be checked at order time.
where: LDO board J5 (DF40C-120DP-0.4V(51)); router J5 (DF40C-120DS-0.4V(51)); LDO board U1 (LT3582EUD-12), D11/D12 (B0540WS-7), L11/L12; J5 Datasheet field on both boards.
evidence: exports/ldo_b_ldo/parts.csv: J5 LCSC empty; LCSC on 5 of 75 parts (U2/U6/U8/U9 C580010, U10 C670492). exports/ldo_b_router/parts.csv: 11 parts, no LCSC column. jlcpcb.com/partdetail/HRS_Hirose-DF40C_120DP_0_4V_51/C22426477: DF40C-120DP-0.4V(51), Extended, SMT assembly; jlcpcb.com/partdetail/C3647197: DF40C-120DS-0.4V(51), Extended. inputs/ldo_a/V12_order/parts_status.csv (10 Nov 16:04): C670975 LT3582 stock 0; C98664 B0540WS-7 stock 0; L11/L12 no part chosen; C2862700 TPS7A2015 55 in stock against 20 needed for 5 boards (not a gap). inputs/ldo_b/V2_record/START_HERE.md line 56: fab files, BOM and placement not made. Both J5 Datasheet URLs end productCode=C3640153, which LCSC lists as DF40GB(1.5)-10DS-0.4V(58).
source: JLCPCB part pages https://jlcpcb.com/partdetail/HRS_Hirose-DF40C_120DP_0_4V_51/C22426477 and https://jlcpcb.com/partdetail/C3647197 ; inputs/ldo_a/V12_order/parts_status.csv.
consequence: A B order cannot be placed until the BOM is mapped, and it will stall on the same out-of-stock U1 and D11/D12 and unchosen L11/L12 as Option A.
suggested_action: Build a B BOM with C22426477 and C3647197 on the two J5 lines and the Option A mapping for the rest, check J5 stock, and add a cross-reference to Option A's open sourcing items in the B record.
verification: Upheld after a third independent check

title: Many MPN fields on the B boards hold a part number plus a description, and 31 BOM lines have no MPN.
what: An MPN (manufacturer part number) field should hold only the orderable number so a BOM tool can match it. On the LDO board, D11/D12, L11/L12 and about 22 capacitors carry a part number followed by a description in brackets. 24 of 66 BOM lines on the LDO board and 7 of 10 on the router have no MPN, and the J1/J2 Mating field still names the old Frontend 8L V1. All of this is copied from Option A.
where: LDO board: D11, D12, L11, L12, capacitors such as C3, C201, C902, C1004; no MPN on C1, C2, C11, C16, C17, C203, C603, C803, R1-R5, R16-R19, R201, R601, R801, R901, R1001, JP1, JP2; J1/J2 Mating field. Router: no MPN on C51, C53-C57, R6.
evidence: exports/ldo_b_ldo/parts.csv: D11 MPN 'Diodes Inc. B0540WS-7 (40 V 0.5 A SOD-323)'; L11 Murata DFE201610E-6R8M=P2 with 'Isat >= 0.6 A', L12 the same part with 'Isat >= 0.8 A'. 75 parts, 9 marked no_bom (NT1 and 8 test points), 66 left, 24 without MPN. exports/ldo_b_router/parts.csv: 11 parts, 1 no_bom, 10 left, 7 without MPN. J1 Mating: 'Artix Frontend 8L V1 J1 DF40C-70DS-0.4V(51)'; the current Frontend is 8L V3. exports/ldo_a/parts.csv has the same values. The different Isat notes follow the different peak currents in the LT3582 note on the LDO board schematic (0.42 A boost, 0.69 A inverter), so they do not conflict, but the shared part must meet 0.8 A. JP1/JP2 are bridged solder jumpers and need no part.
source: Engineering judgement.
consequence: Building the B BOM needs hand mapping, and a part could be ordered from a wrong or partial number.
suggested_action: Put bare MPNs in the MPN field and move notes to Description, fill the missing MPNs, mark JP1/JP2 no_bom, choose one L11/L12 part rated at least 0.8 A, and update the Mating text.

title: The router clears the lower ASIC board's side pin by 0.23 mm nominal; a 0.8 mm ASIC board's pin tail hits it.
what: The lower ASIC board has a one-pin AGND side pin (J1) that sits under the router's narrow part. In the fit model its plastic body top is 1.27 mm above the ASIC board and the router underside is 1.5 mm above it (one DF40 stack height), so the gap is 0.23 mm nominal; Hirose publishes no tolerance on the mated height and the pin has no part number, so the margin cannot be proven. Only the insulating plastic body can reach the router (the metal tops out 0.7 mm lower), so contact cannot short anything, but it could preload or hold slightly open the J4 DF40 joint. Separately, if the ASIC board is made 0.8 mm thick, the upper ASIC board's untrimmed pin tail reaches 0.25 mm into the router's top face; the files cannot settle this, because the board thickness is undecided and the real pin part is not named.
where: Router (ldo_b_router) underside L6 over the pin body at about x 89.20-90.20, y 115.74-116.74 (router frame); ASIC board J1 (top side, net /AGND, at 144.875, 68.28) maps to (90.45, 116.24). L6 lanes over the body: ASIC4_DATA7, ASIC4_DATA8, ASIC4_READ (0.1 mm); ASIC4_DATA6 runs over the lead only. Router top face at the same x, y has no L1 copper; L3 GND and L4 AGND planes inside.
evidence: inputs/ldo_b/V2_fit/fit_b_v2.json: 'ASIC down 1' J1 body z 0.10-1.27, router slab z 1.5-3.1, gap 0.23 mm; 'ASIC up 1' J1 tail z 3.65 at 1.6 mm board thickness. KiCad STEP PinHeader_1x01_P1.00mm_Horizontal: only plastic body above z 0.8 (z 1.17-1.27), highest metal z 0.785, tail tip z -2.55. Tolerance stack (a review working file (not published)): -0.23 mm worst case, -0.02 mm RSS, with the main terms (0-0.2 mm seating, +/-0.10 mm body, per-part DF40 +/-0.15 mm as a stand-in for mated tolerance) assumed. Tail with 0.8 mm board: 2.55 - 0.8 = 1.75 mm against a 1.5 mm gap = 0.25 mm at the chamfered tip. exports/asic/parts.csv: J1 has no MPN. inputs/notes/fpga-ldo-v14.md line 108: ASIC board to be 0.8 mm; inputs/asic/pcbway_fab/PCB-job.gbrjob: BoardThickness 1.6. L6 lanes from a geometry query of exports/ldo_b_router/board.json.
source: Hirose DF40 Series catalog, Jun 2024 edition, p8 (receptacle 1.5 mm stacking, D 1.45 +/-0.15) and p14 (plug 1.14 +/-0.15), no mated-height tolerance published, https://www.hirose.com/en/product/series/DF40 ; KiCad library model PinHeader_1x01_P1.00mm_Horizontal; engineering judgement for seating and body tolerances.
consequence: A tall or high-seated pin can preload or partly open the J4 DF40 joint of the lower ASIC board. With 0.8 mm ASIC boards and an untrimmed tail, the upper ASIC board cannot seat fully on the router.
suggested_action: Before ordering the router, name or measure the real side pin and specify a trimmed tail on the ASIC board (needed anyway for the ASIC-to-ASIC joint at 0.8 mm). Notch the router only if the measured body top exceeds about 1.2 mm.
verification: Upheld after a third independent check

title: The 0.5 mm side gaps beside the router and the lower ASIC board can close under normal outline tolerances.
what: In Option B the router and the Frontend sit side by side at the same height, each located by its own connectors on the LDO board; the lower ASIC board sits beside the LDO board's wide end the same way. Each pair is held only through a chain of two outline tolerances, four connector placements and two DF40 matings. With JLC's regular +/-0.2 mm routed outline on each board and about 0.05 mm per placement and mating, the worst case is about 0.2 mm of interference; a statistical (RSS) sum still leaves about 0.19 mm. The placement and mating figures are assumptions, not datasheet values.
where: Router south edge y 122.935 against Frontend edge y 123.435 (LDO-board frame), overlapping over x 88.675-111.315; lower ASIC board edge y 117.134 against LDO board wide end y 117.634.
evidence: inputs/ldo_b/V2_fit/fit_b_v2.json: gap_router_edge_to_frontend_edge_mm 0.5, gap_lower_asic_board_to_ldo_board_edge_mm 0.5; router and LDO board.json edges agree. Stack: 2 x 0.2 + 4 x 0.05 + 2 x 0.05 = 0.70 mm worst case (-0.20 mm); sqrt(2 x 0.2^2 + 6 x 0.05^2) = 0.31 mm RSS (+0.19 mm).
source: JLCPCB PCB capabilities: routed outline +/-0.2 mm regular, +/-0.1 mm precision, https://jlcpcb.com/capabilities/pcb-capabilities ; engineering judgement for placement and mating play.
consequence: Board edges can bind, side-loading the DF40 joints or stopping full seating.
suggested_action: Order precision routing (+/-0.1 mm) for the router and LDO board, or pull the router's south edge and the LDO board's north edge back by 0.2 mm.

title: Router J5 stays open on the head between sessions, with no cover chosen and no way to clean it.
what: In Option B the router stays on the animal's head, so whenever the LDO board is unplugged its 120-contact J5 receptacle faces hair, bedding, blood and saline. Hirose says the connector resists contamination only when mated, does not recommend washing, and lists no cover, and the project has not decided how J5 is protected. The original concern that residue could turn stimulation on is overstated: the FPGA drives STIM_EN once configured, and before configuration the neighbouring STIM_CLK is not driven either. The same signal order and a 10 V contact between low-voltage rails also exist on LDO board J2 and on the ASIC board's J3/J4, so a J5-only pin re-map would not remove the pattern and is not needed before ordering.
where: Router J5 (DF40C-120DS, underside): J5.115 STIM_EN between J5.113 ASIC1_SYNC and J5.117 STIM_CLK, opposite J5.116 STIM_CHB; J5.119 STIM_START beside STIM_CLK; J5.55 VDD10 between J5.53 DVDD and J5.57 VDD_DRIVER; J5.73 VSS10 between J5.71 ASIC1_DATA4 and J5.75 VDD_ADC. Pull-downs R2-R5 on the LDO board. Same order on LDO board J2.61/63/65/67 and ASIC board J3/J4 pins 49/51/53/55.
evidence: exports/ldo_b_router/pads.csv J5 rows (0.4 mm pitch) give the adjacencies above. exports/ldo_b_ldo/parts.csv: R2-R5 10 k to GND; R901 and R1001 (SET resistors of U9 LT3042 and U10 LT3094) are 100 k, and 100 k x 100 uA SET current = about +10 V and -10 V, not 9 V. Frontend_V46_pins_V2.xdc line 109: STIM_EN on J6, LVCMOS15 (an FPGA output). exports/frontend/pads.csv: U1.J18 PUDC_B tied to VCCO_1V5 through R25 (470 ohm), so configuration pull-ups are off and STIM_CLK floats low through R5 before configuration. ASIC_REFERENCE.md line 68: stimulation needs EN and then a START pulse; U03: ASIC input thresholds unknown. exports/asic/pads.csv: J3/J4 49 CHB, 51 EN, 53 CLK, 55 START, 54 VSS10 between 52 REF_VDD and 56 VDD_ADC. DF40 catalogue: protection only when mated, washing not recommended, 30 mating cycles, no cover listed.
source: Hirose DF40 Series catalogue 2013.11 and Aug 1 2022: p.1 feature 7 (contamination resistance when mated), durability 30 mating cycles, p.16 Operating Precautions 5 (washing not recommended), https://www.hirose.com/en/product/series/DF40 (hirose.com returned 403; read from the catalogue copies); ASIC_REFERENCE.md line 68 and U03; engineering judgement.
consequence: Residue in the open slot can bridge 0.4 mm neighbours, including the +/-10 V contacts next to 0.75-1.6 V rails, when the LDO board is plugged back in. Hirose offers no cleaning method.
suggested_action: Decide how router J5 is covered between sessions (for example a blank DF40C-120DP dummy plug or a sealed cap on the head housing), counting each dummy-plug insertion against the 30 rated mating cycles.
verification: Upheld after a third independent check

title: Mating the LDO board to a powered Frontend dips its 3.3 V rail to about 2.2-2.4 V, below the bucks minimum.
what: The LDO board has about 61 uF of uncharged ceramic capacitance on VIN_3V3 and no inrush limit. If it is mated to a Frontend that is already powered, that capacitance charges from the Frontend's VIN_3V3 rail in a few microseconds, faster than the Frontend regulator U16 can respond, and the shared rail dips to about 2.2-2.4 V. That is below the 2.75 V recommended input minimum of the Frontend's MPM3833C buck modules, but above their typical undervoltage-lockout (UVLO, the voltage where a regulator shuts off) of about 2.1 V, so an FPGA reset is possible with worst-case parts but not likely. In Option B J1/J2 is mated once, unpowered, at assembly, so the realistic exposure is bring-up.
where: LDO board (ldo_b_ldo) VIN_3V3 at J2.68-70: C1 22 uF, C11 4.7 uF, C2 0.1 uF, C201/C601/C801 10 uF, C301/C401/C501/C701 1 uF. Frontend VIN_3V3: output of U16 (MPM3833C); inputs of U2, U3, U4, U13 (MPM3833C, pins 13/14; U2.4 EN), U10 (MP5077 load switch), BIAS pin 4 of U5/U6 (TPS74801).
evidence: exports/ldo_b_ldo/netlist.xml: 60.8 uF nominal on VIN_3V3, none DNP; J2.68-70 are the only power pins on J1/J2. exports/frontend/netlist.xml: 164.07 uF on VIN_3V3 (C1, C12, C21, C75, C85, C102, C208 22 uF; C44, C48 4.7 uF; C103 0.47 uF; C82, C83 0.1 uF). Charge sharing 3.3 x 164.07 / 224.87 = 2.41 V nominal, about 2.2 V with DC-bias loss on the charged 6.3 V 0603 parts; 2.55 V if SWITCHED_3V3 (44.1 uF) back-feeds through U10 (not checked). Series capacitance 44.4 uF, tau about 2-4 us at 50-100 mOhm; energy about 0.24 mJ. exports/ldo_a/netlist.xml: same 60.8 uF on the same pins. Records (inputs/notes/fpga-ldo-v14.md; inputs/ldo_b/history/17_.../START_HERE.md line 9): router stays on the head, LDO + Frontend module is removable at J5. No hot-plug or power-off rule recorded.
source: MPS MPM3833C data sheet Rev 1.0, p.3 (recommended VIN 2.75-6 V) and p.4 (UVLO rising 2.3/2.5/2.75 V, hysteresis 400 mV), https://www.monolithicpower.com/en/products/power-modules/ultra-thin-profile/mpm3833c.html ; Hirose DF40 catalogue (0.3 A rated current per contact, continuous); calculation.
consequence: At bring-up, adding the LDO board to a Frontend running on the HDMI cable can briefly push the Frontend's bucks below their input range and, with worst-case parts, reset the FPGA. Contact damage from the microsecond surge is not shown.
suggested_action: Add a handling rule to the board notes: mate J1/J2 only with the HDMI cable unplugged. No inrush circuit is needed before ordering.
verification: Upheld after a third independent check

title: Under pin map V6 the top chips' own SPI latch and clock get no safe-idle pull, though the schematic's configuration-safety argument relies on one.
what: The LDO-board schematic holds SPI_LATCH low with R18 so that floating SPI lines cannot update the ASICs while the FPGA configures (about 7 s with pull-ups off). On that basis it dropped the clock pull-downs R20-R23. On the received V4 boards the two top chips use their own latch and clock: /T_SPI_LATCH on J3/J4 pin 70 and /T_SPI_CLK on pin 72. Pin map V6 turns these into new FPGA outputs, and no V6 plan adds a pull to them. During configuration the top chips' latch would float, and only CHIP_RESET (R19) would protect them.
where: ASIC V4 top board: /T_SPI_LATCH = J3.70, J4.70 and U01_BCD1/2 SPI_LATCH; /T_SPI_CLK = J3.72, J4.72 and U01_BCD1/2 SPI_CLK. Router V2 today: J3.70 /ASIC7_CLK32MHz_Out and J4.70 /ASIC3_CLK32MHz_Out (J5.90/J5.89); J3.72 /ASIC7_SYNC and J4.72 /ASIC3_SYNC. LDO board V2: R18 10k on /SPI_LATCH_SHARED (pin 61, bottom chips only) and R19 on /CHIP_RESET_SHARED.
evidence: exports/asic_top/netlist.xml and exports/asic_bottom/netlist.xml: the bottom chips' SPI_LATCH is on /SPI_LATCH (pin 61); the top chips' is on /T_SPI_LATCH (pin 70); CHIP_RESET on pin 71 reaches all four chips (RRST_DIGITAL, RST_DRIVER). exports/ldo_b_ldo/netlist.xml: the only pulls are R2-R5 on the STIM lines, R16-R18 pull-downs on FE_RESET, IMP_TST and SPI_LATCH_SHARED (pin 61), and the R19 pull-up on CHIP_RESET_SHARED; router pins 70/72 carry no part. boards/ldo_b_ldo/FPGA_LDO_B_LDO_Layout_V2.kicad_sch, text box 'ASIC CONTROL SAFE IDLE': 'SPI_LATCH (pulled low) blocks any SPI update, so floating clocks have no effect'. known/pinmap_v6_trace.csv: J3/J4.70 TOP_SPI_LATCH (out) and .72 TOP_SPI_CLK (out). The fix-plan critic's V6 list has routes and ball swaps but no pulls. SYS-28: about 7 s of configuration with PUDC_B high. Merge re-check: the nets, the text box and the V6 rows as stated. Known context: SYS-28 lists only the floating lines of pin map V5, and the pair-stacking review (known/pair-stacking.json) found these two top-chip inputs undriven under the current map; neither covers the V6 configuration window.
source: Project files listed above; SYS-28 for configuration time and PUDC_B (AMD UG470, from memory in that record, not re-read here); engineering judgement.
consequence: While the FPGA configures, a floating latch can load whatever floating clock and data shift into the top chips. Whether CHIP_RESET clears that is not documented (ASIC-18).
suggested_action: Add one 10k pull-down per port on the V6 top-chip SPI_LATCH lines, and decide on the top-chip SPI_CLK, on whichever board carries V6 (Option A's LDO board, or the router for Option B, as LDOB-07 suggests).

title: Every live J5 mate or unmate reverses the ASIC power order: +/-10 V is present while the 1.5 V rails are down.
what: At power-up the LDO board brings the 1.5 V rails up first and +/-10 V last. At a live mate the +/-10 V rails, backed by 22-32 uF, reach the ASICs within about a microsecond, while the four TPS7A2015 rails (DVDD, VDD_ADC, VDD_DRIVER, VDD_CGEN), backed by only 1 uF against several uF on the ASIC boards, collapse and take tens to hundreds of microseconds to recharge at the regulator current limit. A rocking mate stretches this to milliseconds because the rails make in pin order, and at a live unmate the core rails drain first while +/-10 V, VDD_CGEN and the references linger. No ASIC document says what mixed power does to the chip.
where: LDO board U3/U4/U5/U7 (TPS7A2015, C302/C402/C502/C702 1 uF), U2/U6/U8 (LT3042, 10 uF), U9/U10 (+/-10 V); J5 row x 87.983-111.583 on router and LDO board; head capacitors on router and ASIC boards.
evidence: Flat mate (sim.py, flat_rows.json): TPS7A2015 rails step to 0.40-0.55 V with 0.1 uF parts, about 0.1 V with 1 uF, 0.03-0.06 V with 4.7 uF; time to half voltage 7.5-115 us and to 90 % 21-181 us (ICL 360-730 mA, 160 mA into a short). VDD10/VSS10 reach 57-97 % within about 1 us. Window with VDD10 or VSS10 above 80 % while a 1.5 V rail is below 50 %: 7-9 us (0.1 uF parts), 23-27 us (0.47 uF), 33-38 us (1 uF), 30-55 us (4.7 uF). With 2.2-4.7 uF parts VDD_FE, REF_VDD and VDD10 may recover over 4-80 ms if their SET-to-OUTS clamp conducts near 0.7 V (voltage not stated). Rocking (pads.csv x): west end first gives DVDD, then VDD_CGEN/VDD10/VDD_DRIVER/REF_VCM at the AGND contact, then VDD_FE, REF_VDD, VSS10, VDD_ADC 1.6-2.8 mm further along the 23.6 mm row, so +10 V sits on the ASICs without -10 V or VDD_ADC; east end first gives VDD_ADC/VSS10/REF_VDD/VDD_FE first and VDD10, DVDD later, VDD_CGEN 12 mm later. Unmate (budget loads x4, 1 uF parts): half voltage VDD_FE 0.51 ms, VDD_ADC 0.52 ms, VDD_DRIVER 1.5 ms, DVDD 1.7 ms, VDD_CGEN 12-120 ms, VDD10/VSS10 1.5 ms at 2 mA/board up to 0.3 s at 10 uA/board, REF rails unknown (TBD); all scale with the capacitor value. With 0.22-0.47 ohm added in every rail the head rails become monotonic but the 8-46 us inversion remains (mono2_out.txt).
source: TI TPS7A20 data sheet SBVS338H (Jul 2024) p.7 (ICL, ISC) and section 6.3.4 p.24, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tps7a20.pdf; ADI LT3042 Rev B (3042fb) p.4 (internal current limit 220/300/320 mA; Note 7 SET/OUTS clamp) and p.19, read from saved copy a review working file (not published) because https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/lt3042.pdf timed out; inputs/asic/J3_pinout__Power_Budget.csv; inputs/asic/ASIC_Reference/ASIC_REFERENCE.md lines 174-179 (U02, U03, U07 'unspecified mixed-power ... behavior'); known SYS-50 and LDOA-28.
consequence: The ASICs see their stimulator rails without their digital and analogue core supplies: microseconds per flat mate, milliseconds per rocking mate, up to about a second after an unmate. Latch-up or an undefined stimulator state cannot be excluded.
suggested_action: Make the LDOB-04 rule firm: unplug the HDMI cable at the stack, wait at least 10 s, mate or unmate J5 parallel, plug the cable last; capacitor or damping choices cannot fix the order. Enforce it at the next J5 re-pin (needed for pin map V6 and LDOB-24) with a mate-detect loop through the two end columns that holds EN_ASIC_RAILS low (add a 10 kOhm pull-down) until both ends are seated, and ask the ASIC designer which mixed-power states are allowed.

title: A live J5 mate drives 23-135 A through each +/-10 V contact and up to 111 A through the single AGND contact J5.62, which are rated 0.25 A with no surge or live-insertion rating.
what: Each rail's charge-sharing surge flows through its one DF40 contact and returns through J5.62, the only AGND contact for eight rails. Peaks are 10-500 times the continuous rating for 0.1-2 us. Heating of the contact body is negligible, but up to about 0.24 mJ per +/-10 V rail is released while the contact is still closing. Hirose gives no make-current, surge or live-insertion rating for DF40, and J5 is rated for 30 mating cycles.
where: J5 rail contacts 2, 53, 55, 57, 60, 70, 72, 73, 75 on router J5 (DF40C-120DS) and LDO J5 (DF40C-120DP); return J5.62 (AGND, x 99.983) for eight rails; J5.3/J5.65 (GND) for DVDD.
evidence: Flat mate, typical corner with 0.1-4.7 uF parts [range over R/L corners] (flat_rows.json, rail_table_flat.csv): VDD10 37-67 A [23-120], VSS10 42-76 A [26-135], VDD_FE and REF_VDD 5-7 A [2.4-16], DVDD 6.0-6.5 A [3.4-10.5], VDD_DRIVER 4.2-4.7 A [2.1-8.1], VDD_ADC 3.7-4.3 A [2.0-7.1], VDD_CGEN 2.1-2.4 A [1.3-4.1], REF_VCM 1.8-2.6 A [0.7-6.6]. Half-amplitude width 0.12-0.54 us (+/-10 V), 0.16-1.9 us (others). I2t: +/-10 V 1.4e-4 to 2.4e-3 A2s [6e-5 to 5e-3], others 1e-6 to 1.2e-4 A2s, against 0.0625 A2s for one second at 0.25 A, so body heating is not the issue. J5.62: 16-17 A [7-35] in a flat mate, where VDD10 and VSS10 partly cancel; 34-111 A when one +/-10 V rail makes alone in a rocking mate (rock_out.txt). Energy released per mate in each +/-10 V loop: 17 uJ (0.1 uF parts), 97-102 uJ (1 uF), 214-244 uJ (4.7 uF). In the low-resistance corner the 1 uF DVDD output (U5 OUT) also rings to -0.34 to -0.64 V for about 0.1 us, past the TPS7A20 -0.3 V absolute minimum. Series damping (0.22-0.47 ohm per 1.5 V rail, 0.47-1 ohm per +/-10 V rail) lowers peaks to 1-4.5 A and 7-19 A, still above the rating.
source: Hirose DF40 Series catalogue (Feb 2024, (c) Jun 1 2024) p.5 Product Specifications (0.3 A; Note 1: 0.25 A for 120 positions; 50 V; 90 mOhm max at 1 mA; 30 mating cycles) and pp.21-23 precautions, LCSC-hosted copy https://datasheet.lcsc.com/datasheet/pdf/145ab5d527b34eafa7a47375cb561c6a.pdf?productCode=C3640153 (https://www.hirose.com/en/product/series/DF40 returned 403; the 120-position spec sheets were not re-read). TI TPS7A20 SBVS338H p.5 absolute maximum VOUT -0.3 V, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tps7a20.pdf. Contact-spot heating at make is engineering judgement from memory, not re-read.
consequence: Repeated live mating may pit or weld contact surfaces and wear the 30-cycle plating early; a degraded J5.62 would float the analogue ground of every ASIC (LDOB-02). Damage is not shown, because Hirose publishes no rating for this case.
suggested_action: Prevent live mating by the rule in the previous finding. If it must be tolerated, ask Hirose for a make-current rating for DF40C-120 and add series damping and more AGND contacts at the next J5 re-pin.

title: With ASIC capacitors of about 1-2 uF or more, a live J5 mate pulls the Frontend's 3.3 V input below its buck modules' range.
what: At a live mate the seven VIN_3V3-fed regulators hit current limit together and refill the head capacitors in 0.05-0.15 ms, drawing about 1.5-4 A through the three J2 power contacts. The HDMI port switch is already close to its limit, so the charge must come from the Frontend's 3.3 V and 5 V capacitors. With 0.47 uF or smaller parts this fits; 1 uF parts use the budget up; with 2.2 uF or more it exceeds what the Frontend can give before its MPM3833C modules reach undervoltage lockout, so the FPGA resets and the head goes through an uncontrolled power cycle.
where: LDO board VIN_3V3 at J2.68-70; Frontend U16 (VIN_5V to VIN_3V3), U2/U3/U4/U13 (MPM3833C on VIN_3V3); VIN_5V C206/C207; VIN_3V3 C1, C12, C21, C75, C85, C102, C208, C44, C48.
evidence: Charge that ends on the head capacitors from the VIN_3V3-fed rails (typical derating): 20 uC (0.1 uF parts), 35 uC (0.22), 63 uC (0.47), 112 uC (1 uF), 201 uC (2.2), 354 uC (4.7), plus 35-730 uC for the +/-10 V refill through the LT3582 over about a millisecond. Sum of current limits 2.1-3.9 A (TPS7A20 p.7, LT3042 p.4). Frontend VIN_3V3 164 uF nominal plus LDO board 60.8 uF, about 114 uF effective at 3.3 V (6.3 V 0603 GRM188R60J226MEA0D taken at about 45 %, from memory); VIN_5V 44 uF nominal, about 20 uF effective. Charge available before VIN_3V3 falls to 2.75 V: about 98 uC; to 2.35 V (worst-case falling UVLO, 2.75 V rising maximum less 0.4 V hysteresis): about 143 uC. J2.68-70 are DF40C-70 contacts rated 0.3 A each.
source: MPS MPM3833C data sheet Rev 1.0 p.1 (VIN 2.75-6 V) and p.4 (UVLO rising 2.3/2.5/2.75 V, hysteresis 400 mV; P-FET current limit 3.6 A min), https://www.monolithicpower.com/en/documentview/productdocument/index/version/2/document_type/Datasheet/lang/en/sku/MPM3833CGRH-Z/document_id/4426/ (read from saved copy a review working file (not published)); exports/frontend/netlist.xml; exports/ldo_b_ldo/netlist.xml; known FE-02 (port margin 0.02-0.10 A) and SYS-46 (TPS2553 limit 636-763 mA).
consequence: If 1 uF or larger ASIC capacitors are chosen, every live J5 mate would also reset the Frontend; the J1/J2 dip of LDOB-12 is not the only exposure in Option B.
suggested_action: Covered by the cable-off rule; when the ASIC capacitor values are chosen, record that 1 uF or larger parts turn a live mate into a Frontend reset.

title: After the HDMI cable is pulled, the LDO board's +/-10 V outputs stay charged for seconds, so 'cable off' alone does not make a quick re-mate safe.
what: The fix planned for LDOB-04 is a 'cable last on, first off' rule. When the cable is pulled, VDD10 on the LDO board has no bleed: U9 blocks reverse current and the only drain is its SET pin path through R901 (100 kOhm), a time constant of about 1 s; VSS10 drains only with STIM_PRE_NEG. A module unplugged and re-mated to a cold head within a few seconds therefore repeats the surge and overshoot, with +/-10 V and no 1.5 V rails at all and no regulator running.
where: LDO board U9, C902, C903, R901 (ASIC_VDD10); U10, C1002, C1004, C1003, R1001 (ASIC_VSS10); C901/C14 and C1001/C21 on STIM_PRE_POS/NEG.
evidence: LT3042 p.4: reverse output current 2/5 uA (VIN 0 V, VOUT 5 V, SET open); p.19: overshoot-recovery sink disabled below VIN 2.5 V; p.22: with the input pulled to ground the output is held up, current flows only through the SET resistor (via the OUTS-to-SET clamp) and the overshoot circuit. tau about 100 kOhm x (C902 about 10 uF effective + C903 1 uF) = 1.1 s: VDD10 about 4 V at 1 s, 1.6 V at 2 s, near the clamp offset after about 5 s. Known LDOA-28 power-down model (same circuit): VDD10 still 10.00 V and VSS10 -8.2 to -9.5 V at 0.8 s with no load. The 1.5 V LT3042 outputs drain in about 0.15 s (15 kOhm). A charged 8-10 V source into a cold head gives the same ringing as finding 1.
source: ADI LT3042 Rev B pp.4, 19, 22 (saved copy a review working file (not published); https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/lt3042.pdf timed out); ADI LT3094 Rev 0 p.6 Note 2 (OUT-to-IN parasitic diodes) and p.28 (saved copy a review working file (not published); https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/lt3094.pdf); known LDOA-28; known/fix_plans_11nov_evening_on_V3.json item LDOB-04.
consequence: A handler who swaps modules quickly with the cable off can still put charged +/-10 V rails on a cold head; the routine cable-pull power-down also carries LDOA-28's lingering +/-10 V on Option B, which has the same circuit.
suggested_action: Write the rule as 'cable off, wait at least 10 s, then mate or unmate J5 parallel, cable on last', or add a 10-22 kOhm bleed from ASIC_VDD10 and ASIC_VSS10 to AGND on the LDO board (5-10 mW), which also serves LDOA-28.

title: J5 footprints are unchecked against Hirose's 120-pin drawings, and DF40 Datasheet links name another part.
what: The 120-pin J5 footprints on both B boards were drawn the same way as the 70- and 80-pin DF40 footprints, not copied from Hirose's 120-pin customer drawings. Their pad rows and body lengths match the catalogue formulas and Hirose's product pages, but the Fab-layer body widths are narrower than Hirose lists, and the stack fit test used those footprint bodies. Separately, the Datasheet field on every DF40 connector links an LCSC page for a shielded 10-pin part, so anyone following it reads the wrong drawing.
where: Router J5 (Hirose_DF40C-120DS-0.4V_2x60_P0.4mm, bottom); LDO board J5 (Hirose_DF40C-120DP-0.4V_2x60-1MP_P0.4mm, top). Datasheet field on router J3/J4/J5, LDO board J1/J2/J5, and the four DF40 connectors in Option A.
evidence: Router library FPGA_LDO_V33B_Router.pretty/Hirose_DF40C-120DS-0.4V_2x60_P0.4mm.kicad_mod: 120 pads 0.20 x 0.70 mm at y +/-1.54, x -11.8 to 11.8 (B = 23.6 mm); Fab body 26.6 x 2.88 mm. LDO library FPGA_LDO_V33B_LDO.pretty/Hirose_DF40C-120DP-0.4V_2x60-1MP_P0.4mm.kicad_mod: 120 pads 0.23 x 0.66 mm at y +/-1.355, 4 corner pads 0.35 x 0.66 mm at x +/-12.275; Fab body 25.52 x 1.85 mm. Catalogue formulas: DS A = 0.2n + 2.6 = 26.6, B = 0.2n - 0.4 = 23.6; DP A = 0.2n + 1.52 = 25.52. Hirose product pages (from search summaries): CL0684-4108-1-51 (DS) 26.6 x 3.38 mm, 1.45 mm high; CL0684-4107-9-51 (DP) 25.52 x 2.97 x 1.14 mm. exports/ldo_b_router/parts.csv and exports/ldo_b_ldo/parts.csv Datasheet = ...productCode=C3640153 (4 matching rows in exports/ldo_a/parts.csv); the LCSC C3640153 page is DF40GB(1.5)-10DS-0.4V(58), 10 pins. The Hirose customer drawings were not opened.
source: Hirose DF40 catalogue (Aug 1 2022), p.4 receptacle 1.5 mm table and recommended PCB layout, p.10 header table and layout; Hirose product pages https://www.hirose.com/en/product/p/CL0684-4108-1-51 and https://www.hirose.com/en/product/p/CL0684-4107-9-51 (403 to automated reads; values from search summaries); https://www.lcsc.com/product-detail/C3640153.html.
consequence: Low risk: if the 120-pin part differs in pad pattern or corner fittings, J5 will not solder or mate, and the narrower bodies make the fit model slightly optimistic. Anyone using the Datasheet link reads the wrong part.
suggested_action: Get the Hirose customer drawings for 684-4108-1 and 684-4107-9, confirm the pad rows, B = 23.6 mm, the corner pads and the body widths, and point the Datasheet fields at those drawings.

title: VDD_ADC, VDD10 and VSS10 lack router capacitors; their nearest capacitor is now behind J5, 12-16 mm away.
what: The router has a 1 uF capacitor on six ASIC rails next to J3/J4, as Option A does. VDD_ADC, VDD10 and VSS10 had no local capacitor on Option A either, but there the regulator's output capacitor sat 7-11 mm away on the same board. On Option B it is 12-16 mm away and behind one J5 contact. The ASIC board carries its own capacitors on all three rails, so this is not expected to matter.
where: Router V2 nets /ASIC_VDD_ADC, /ASIC_VDD10, /ASIC_VSS10 (router capacitors C51, C53-C57 are on the other six rails); LDO board V2 C302 (VDD_ADC), C902 (VDD10), C1004 (VSS10, 10 uF).
evidence: Straight-line pad-to-pad distances, not copper path lengths, from exports/*/pads.csv. Router J5 to J3/J4: 3.60 mm. Option A, capacitor to J4: C302 10.86 mm, C902 8.24 mm, C1004 6.74 mm. Option B, LDO capacitor to J5: C302 12.47 mm, C902 10.20 mm, C1004 8.93 mm, giving 16.1 / 13.8 / 12.5 mm in total. The first pass used C1002 for VSS10 (9.8 mm on A, 15.1 mm on B); C1004 is on the same rail and closer. exports/asic/pads.csv: /VDD_ADC C1, C34; /VDD10 C18, C19; /VSS10 C25, C26.
source: Engineering judgement.
consequence: Slightly higher supply impedance at the ASIC connector for fast load steps on these three rails.
suggested_action: No change needed. If space allows, add a 1 uF capacitor on each of these three rails at router J3/J4.

title: Seven clock segments run directly over or under another signal on the next layer, only 0.071 mm away.
what: On the router, layers L1/L2 and L5/L6 have no plane between them, and the same holds for L1/L2 on the LDO board. Where a trace on one layer sits directly on top of a trace on the next layer (broadside coupling), the coupling is strong: the backward coupling coefficient Kb, the fraction of the aggressor's edge that appears on the victim, is about 0.25 to 0.32. The overlaps are only 1.4 to 2.3 mm long, so each adds at most a few tens of millivolts. For the CLK32 pairs, which run in the same direction as the data they overlap, the noise reaches the receiver only after a partial reflection at the ASIC driver, so about 15 to 25 mV is more likely than the doubled upper bound.
where: Router: ASIC2 CLK32 (L5) under ASIC4 CLK32 (L6), 1.5 to 1.6 mm; ASIC5 CLK32 (L1) over ASIC5_DATA2, 1.36 mm; BOARD1_SPI_CLK (L5) under ASIC3_DATA7, 1.78 mm; BOARD3_SPI_CLK (L2) under ASIC7_DATA7, 1.97 mm. LDO board: ASIC3 CLK32 (L2) under ASIC7_DATA8, 2.29 mm; ASIC5 CLK32 (L1) over ASIC5_DATA4, 1.44 mm; ASIC7 CLK32 (L1) over ASIC3_DATA8, 1.39 mm.
evidence: Overlap lengths from board.json (exports/ldo_b_router, exports/ldo_b_ldo), counting adjacent-layer tracks whose centrelines lie within the sum of half-widths, sampled every 0.01 mm; the re-check reproduced every length within 0.05 mm. Layer gap 0.071 mm (1078 prepreg) from inputs/ldo_a/V12_checks/JLC_stackup_JLCH061611Y1-1078.json. Field solve at zero offset: Kb 0.319 (router), 0.251 (LDO board). Near-end noise is about Kb x 2TD/tr x 1.5 V; for 2.29 mm, 2TD is about 29 ps, giving about 47 mV at a 0.5 ns edge and 23 mV at 1 ns if doubled at an open end. The doubling applies directly only to the two SPI_CLK segments.
source: Engineering judgement.
consequence: Small additions to the clock noise totals on both boards; no action needed on its own.
suggested_action: If these lanes are re-routed for other findings, shift these segments sideways by about 0.3 mm so they no longer sit on top of each other.

title: A 180-degree placement error on any DF40 connector cannot swap nets, so the connector risk in LDOA-24 does not exist.
what: LDOA-24 says a DF40 placed 180 degrees wrong would put VIN_3V3 on signal pins, by mapping pin n to pin 71-n. That mapping applies when a mated board is turned round, not when a part is turned on its own pads. The DF40 header and receptacle have no polarity and identical contacts in symmetric positions, so a rotated part still joins each pad to the contact directly above it and the nets cannot change. The placement check still matters for the polarized parts (U1-U10, D11, D12). The same applies to the B boards' J1/J2/J5 and the router's J3/J4/J5 when their order files are made. Board rotation (SYS-09) is a different, real risk.
where: Option B LDO board J1, J2 (DF40C-70DP) and J5 (DF40C-120DP); router J3 (80DP), J4 (80DS) and J5 (120DS); Option A J1-J4.
evidence: The pad patterns are symmetric under a 180-degree turn. For example, LDO J5 contacts span x 87.983-111.583 (centre 99.783) with rows at y 118.845/121.555 (centre 120.2), and MP pads sit at x 87.508/112.058 in both rows (exports/ldo_b_ldo/pads.csv). Router J5 rows are at y 118.66/121.74. A part turned about its centre puts a contact on every pad, and each pad keeps its net. Merge re-check: under a 180-degree turn about (99.783, 120.2) both J5 pad sets map onto themselves in position and size (LDO board 120 pads plus 4 MP, router 120 pads).
source: Hirose DF40 catalogue, 1 Jun 2024: p.8 receptacle table note 4 and p.14 plug table note 5 (the connector has no polarity); p.14 note 3 (four corner fittings, not energized). https://www.hirose.com/en/product/series/DF40 (saved copy a review working file (not published); hirose.com returned 403). Project record LDOA-24 (known/ldo_a.json).
consequence: Time spent checking DF40 rotation in JLC's placement review is wasted; the real placement risk is on polarized parts only.
suggested_action: Close the connector part of LDOA-24 and keep the placement check for U1-U10 and D11/D12 on both options.

title: The Frontend's J2 receptacle ends only 0.21 mm from R4's pad on the LDO board, leaving little margin.
what: The project record checked R4 only against the LDO board's own J2 plug, using an assumed length. The closer part is the Frontend FPGA Board's DF40C-70DS receptacle, which mates over LDO J2 and hangs down to about 0.05 mm above the LDO board. With Hirose's drawn length of 16.6 mm it stops 0.21 mm short of R4's pad in plan view, so there is no overlap and the stack fits as drawn. The margin is small: at the +0.2 mm length tolerance the pad gap falls to about 0.11 mm.
where: LDO board top side: R4 (0402, centre 110.5, 123.52, rotation -90), pads y 122.74 to 124.30, x 110.18 to 110.82; body about y 123.02 to 124.02. Frontend J2 (DF40C-70DS-0.4V(51), bottom side, rotation 90) mated over LDO J2 (centre 108.755, 132.81): receptacle body x 107.07 to 110.45, y 124.51 to 141.11.
evidence: exports/ldo_b_ldo/pads.csv: R4 pads at (110.5, 123.01) and (110.5, 124.03), 0.54 x 0.64 mm; J2 pads x 107.4 to 110.11, y 125.535 to 140.085, centre (108.755, 132.81). exports/ldo_b_ldo/parts.csv: J2 and R4 top, rotation -90. exports/frontend/parts.csv: J2 bottom, rotation 90. Hirose DF40C-70DS: A = 16.6 +/-0.2 mm, width 3.38 +/-0.2 mm, height 1.45 mm in a 1.5 mm stack (catalogue p8). Receptacle end 132.81 - 8.30 = 124.51; gap to R4 pad 124.51 - 124.30 = 0.21 mm; to R4 body 124.51 - 124.02 = 0.49 mm. For comparison the LDO board's own DF40C-70DP plug (A = 15.52, p14) ends at y 125.05, 0.75 mm from R4's pad.
source: Hirose DF40 Series catalogue, 1 June 2024 edition, p8 (receptacle, 1.5 mm stacking height) and p14 (plug); https://www.hirose.com/en/product/series/DF40
consequence: None if the parts land as drawn. A placement or body-length error of about 0.2 mm would put the receptacle onto R4's solder fillet.
suggested_action: No change needed now. If the Frontend J2 placement changes, re-check this gap or move R4 0.2 mm north.

title: The Option B records rate each J5 contact at 0.3 A, but Hirose rates the 120-position DF40 at 0.25 A.
what: Each of the nine ASIC rails crosses J5 on one contact, and the return uses two GND contacts and one AGND contact. The B records use 0.3 A per contact, but the current Hirose DF40 catalogue gives 0.25 A for the 120-position size. With the ASIC designer's power budget, every contact still carries under 20 % of 0.25 A, so nothing needs to change in the layout now. REF_VDD and REF_VCM currents are still marked TBD in that budget.
where: J5 (router DF40C-120DS, LDO board DF40C-120DP): rails on pins 2 (VDD_CGEN), 53 (DVDD), 55 (VDD10), 57 (VDD_DRIVER), 60 (REF_VCM), 70 (VDD_FE), 72 (REF_VDD), 73 (VSS10), 75 (VDD_ADC); GND on 3 and 65; AGND on 62.
evidence: exports/ldo_b_router/pads.csv and exports/ldo_b_ldo/pads.csv J5 rows match inputs/ldo_b/V2_record/J5_pin_map_V4.csv; the four retention pads (MP) have no net, so J5.2 is a real contact. Hirose DF40 catalogue, 1 Jun 2024, p.5: rated current 0.3 A, Note 1 gives 0.25 A for 120 positions; the Aug 2022 and 2013 catalogues give 0.3 A with no such note. inputs/asic/J3_pinout__Power_Budget.csv per board: VDD_FE 4.53 mA, VDD_ADC 4.18, VDD_DRIVER 1.51, DVDD 1.39 mA; VDD10/VSS10 2 mA max each; VDD_CGEN under 100 uA; REF TBD. For four boards: VDD_FE 18.1 mA (7 % of 0.25 A); summed 1.5 V current 46.4 mA (19 %).
source: Hirose DF40 series catalogue, 1 Jun 2024, p.5, ratings Note 1 (0.25 A for 120 positions), https://www.hirose.com/en/product/pr/df40/
consequence: None at the supplied budget. If the REF currents or measured rail currents turn out much higher, a contact could exceed its rating and the rail would drop across the connector.
suggested_action: Change the 0.3 A figure in the Option B records to 0.25 A, and recheck the J5 margin once the REF_VDD and REF_VCM currents are known or measured at bring-up.

title: Both J5 footprints match Hirose's 120-position drawings, but their Datasheet field links a 10-position part.
what: An earlier finding said the two J5 footprints had not been checked against a 120-position drawing. Both now match Hirose's recommended PCB patterns: pad size, row offset, pitch, span, fitting (hold-down) pads, body outline and pin 1. All 120 pins also line up with the same position, row and net on both boards. What remains is that the Datasheet field on both J5 parts points to LCSC C3640153, which is a 10-position DF40GB part, not either 120-position part.
where: Router J5 (Hirose_DF40C-120DS-0.4V_2x60_P0.4mm, bottom layer); LDO board J5 (Hirose_DF40C-120DP-0.4V_2x60-1MP_P0.4mm).
evidence: Router (exports/ldo_b_router/pads.csv): 120 pads 0.20 x 0.70 mm at y +/-1.54, pitch 0.4, span 23.6 mm, no fitting pads; DS drawing pattern (3.78 - 2.38)/2 = 0.70 long, centred at 1.54. LDO board (exports/ldo_b_ldo/pads.csv): 120 pads 0.23 x 0.66 at +/-1.355 plus four MP pads 0.35 x 0.66 at x 87.508 and 112.058 (+/-12.275 from 99.783), no net; DP drawing (3.37 - 2.05)/2 = 0.66 at 1.355, MP at 11.8 + 0.475 = 12.275. Fab outlines 26.6 x 2.88 mm (DS) and 25.52 x 1.85 mm (DP), matching the drawings. Pin 1 at x 87.983 on both; 120/120 pins share x, row and net. parts.csv Datasheet on both J5 = LCSC C3640153 = DF40GB(1.5)-10DS-0.4V(58).
source: Hirose customer drawings EDC-317850-51-00 rev 0 (DF40C-120DS-0.4V(51)) and EDC-317849-51-00 rev 1 (DF40C-120DP-0.4V(51)), sheet 1, recommended PCB pattern; https://www.hirose.com/en/product/p/CL0684-4108-1-51 and https://www.hirose.com/en/product/p/CL0684-4107-9-51
consequence: The J5 land patterns will accept and mate the real parts. The wrong Datasheet link can mislead anyone checking or sourcing J5.
suggested_action: Replace each J5 Datasheet field with the matching Hirose drawing number and part page, and record both drawing numbers in the B record.
